nodes.title: World Settings & Gamerules
nodes.tagline: Every Solo Leveling gamerule, what it does, and its default
nodes.summary: Change '31 gamerules' to '32 gamerules'. Most of them are set from the Solo Leveling tab when you create a world, and every one of them can be changed later with the vanilla /gamerule command.

facts.label: soloLevelingStoryMode (default false)
facts.value: Starts new players with the Solo Leveling story introduction. Designed for single-player.

facts.label: soloLevelingProgressionPreset (default 0)
facts.value: Records the world-creation progression preset: 0 Standard, 1 Fast, 2 Custom. Bookkeeping only; the child rules below hold the real values.

facts.label: soloLevelingDifficultyPreset (default 0)
facts.value: Records the world-creation difficulty preset: 0 Normal, 1 Hard, 2 Brutal, 3 Custom. Bookkeeping only.

facts.label: soloLevelingXPMultiplier (default 10)
facts.value: XP multiplier for mod XP. 10 = 1.0x, 15 = 1.5x, 20 = 2.0x.

facts.label: soloLevelingJobChangeLevel (default 40)
facts.value: The level at which the Job Change quest unlocks. Valid range 20-100.

facts.label: soloLevelingLevelCap (default 150)
facts.value: The peak of the progression curve. 0 = unlimited levelling; anything above 300 is treated as 300. Reaching the cap ends levelling and opens the return to the Cartenon Temple.

facts.label: soloLevelingEnemyScale (default 100)
facts.value: Solo Leveling enemy health and damage as a percentage. Clamped to 25-400 at runtime.

facts.label: soloLevelingBossPower (default 100)
facts.value: Additional boss health, damage, and resistance as a percentage. Clamped to 25-400 at runtime.

facts.label: soloLevelingRankedGates (default true)
facts.value: Limits natural gate ranks to the target player's Solo Leveling progression. Set false to allow every gate rank.

facts.label: soloLevelingDeathRules (default 0)
facts.value: Dungeon death handling: 0 Standard, 1 Forgiving, 2 Harsh. See the Death Rules page.

facts.label: soloLevelingMonarchLimit (default 1)
facts.value: How many players may hold the same Ruler or Monarch vessel. 0 = unlimited.

facts.label: soloLevelingJobChangePoints (default 50)
facts.value: Knight kills required to complete the Job Change advancement trial.

facts.label: soloLevelingLoreAccurateRanks (default true)
facts.value: Makes the difference between the starting Hunter ranks larger when enabled.

facts.label: soloLevelingRankOddsE (default 25)
facts.value: Awakening weight for E rank. Weights are raw values, not literal percentages; all six are rescaled to total 100 when an evaluation rolls.

facts.label: soloLevelingRankOddsD (default 25)
facts.value: Awakening weight for D rank.

facts.label: soloLevelingRankOddsC (default 25)
facts.value: Awakening weight for C rank.

facts.label: soloLevelingRankOddsB (default 12)
facts.value: Awakening weight for B rank.

facts.label: soloLevelingRankOddsA (default 10)
facts.value: Awakening weight for A rank.

facts.label: soloLevelingRankOddsS (default 3)
facts.value: Awakening weight for S rank. With the defaults the six weights total exactly 100, so S = 3%.

facts.label: disableBlockBreaking (default false)
facts.value: When true, cancels block breaking and placing for players who are currently inside a dungeon run.

facts.label: soloDailyQuest (default true)
facts.value: Enables or disables Daily Quests given by the System.

facts.label: soloDungeonProgressionOnly (default true)
facts.value: When enabled you only gain mod XP from dungeon monsters.

facts.label: soloFatigue (default true)
facts.value: Enables or disables Fatigue buildup.

facts.label: soloAbilityDestruction (default false)
facts.value: Legacy on/off switch for ability terrain damage. Kept so old worlds load with their existing preference; new worlds should use soloAbilityDestructionMode.

facts.label: soloAbilityDestructionMode (default -1)
facts.value: Three-mode terrain damage setting: 0 = off, 1 = partial (outside dungeons only), 2 = on. -1 means an older world has not chosen yet, so the legacy boolean decides. Red Gates and the Demon King's Castle are always protected.

facts.label: soloGateNotification (default true)
facts.value: Toggles the chat notification sent when a new gate appears.

facts.label: soloGateDelay (default 400)
facts.value: Minimum time in seconds between natural gate spawns. The timer ticks once per second in the overworld.

facts.label: soloGateSpawning (default true)
facts.value: Toggles natural gate spawning entirely.

facts.label: soloMiscItems (default true)
facts.value: Toggles whether misc items are offered in the System shop.

facts.label: soloDungeonBreak (default true)
facts.value: Toggles dungeon breaks (gates erupting when left alone).

facts.label: soloBloodEffects (default true)
facts.value: Toggles blood visual effects.

facts.label: soloPunishment (default true)
facts.value: Toggles the punishment players receive when they do not complete their Daily Quest.

sections.heading: Where you set these
sections.body: When you create a world, a Solo Leveling tab appears in the world creation screen. It exposes Story Mode, Ability Destruction, the Progression and Difficulty preset columns, and an Awakening Odds editor. Everything it writes is a normal gamerule stored with that world. After the world exists, change any value with /gamerule, for example: /gamerule soloLevelingXPMultiplier 15. Changes apply immediately; nothing needs a restart.

sections.heading: Presets versus individual rules
sections.body: soloLevelingProgressionPreset and soloLevelingDifficultyPreset only record which preset button was chosen. The child rules (XP multiplier, job change level, enemy scale, boss power, death rules, ranked gates) hold the values the game actually reads. If you edit a child rule by hand, the recorded preset simply stops matching; the tab will show Custom the next time it reads the world.

sections.heading: Ability destruction
sections.body: Terrain damage from high-impact abilities has three modes. Off (0) is the safe default: abilities never damage terrain. Partial (1) lets abilities damage eligible terrain outside dungeons only. On (2) allows it everywhere eligible. In every mode, Red Gates and the Demon King's Castle are protected. Old worlds that only have the legacy soloAbilityDestruction boolean keep their behavior: the mode rule stays at -1 and the boolean decides.

sections.heading: Awakening odds
sections.body: The six soloLevelingRankOdds rules are weights, not percentages. Each weight is clamped to 0-100, then all six are rescaled so they total 100 when a Hunter evaluation rolls a rank. Example from the code: weights of 25/25/25/12/12/11 total 110 and give S a real chance of 10%. The world creation tab has an Awakening Odds screen that edits these and shows the normalized S chance on its button.

nodes.title: Difficulty Presets
nodes.tagline: Normal, Hard, Brutal, Custom - and exactly what each changes
nodes.summary: The Difficulty column of the world creation tab bundles three settings: Enemy Scale, Boss Power, and Death Rules. A preset just writes fixed values into those three gamerules; you can mix your own values and the preset becomes Custom.

facts.label: Normal (id 0)
facts.value: Enemy Scale 100%, Boss Power 100%, Death Rules Standard.

facts.label: Hard (id 1)
facts.value: Enemy Scale 125%, Boss Power 125%, Death Rules Standard. Enemies and bosses gain 25% health and damage.

facts.label: Brutal (id 2)
facts.value: Enemy Scale 150%, Boss Power 150%, Death Rules Harsh. Enemies and bosses gain 50% power and Harsh dungeon deaths apply.

facts.label: Custom (id 3)
facts.value: Keeps whatever individual values you set.

facts.label: UI choices
facts.value: The creation tab offers 100/125/150 for both Enemy Scale (labeled Standard/High/Extreme) and Boss Power (Standard/+25%/+50%). Via /gamerule you can use any value; the game clamps to 25-400% at runtime.

facts.label: Boss extras at +50% (Brutal)
facts.value: +50% max health and attack damage, +4 armor, +2 armor toughness, +0.1 knockback resistance.

sections.heading: How Enemy Scale is applied
sections.body: When a Solo Leveling enemy spawns or loads, the mod attaches attribute modifiers for max health and attack damage sized by (percent/100 - 1). At 100% no modifier is added. The mob's current health percentage is preserved when its max health changes, so already-damaged mobs stay proportionally damaged. The modifiers use stable IDs, so re-loading a chunk replaces them instead of stacking them.

sections.heading: How Boss Power is applied
sections.body: Bosses get the same health and damage multiplier as Enemy Scale, but from the separate soloLevelingBossPower rule, plus flat bonuses that scale with the same amount: armor (8 x amount), armor toughness (4 x amount), and knockback resistance (0.2 x amount). Example at 150%: amount is 0.5, so a boss gets +50% health and damage, +4 armor, +2 toughness, and +0.1 knockback resistance.

sections.heading: Who counts as an enemy or a boss
sections.body: The scaling targets mobs from this mod, mobs spawned by the dungeon runtime, and mobs added to the soloboss or dm entity-type tags (datapacks can use these tags to opt other mods' monsters in). A mob counts as a boss if it is in the soloboss tag or the dungeon runtime marked its role as boss. Your own side is excluded: hunters, shadow soldiers, tamed animals, and owned summons are never scaled up, and cosmetic entities such as visual effects and the training bot are skipped.

sections.heading: Changing difficulty later
sections.body: Use /gamerule soloLevelingEnemyScale, /gamerule soloLevelingBossPower, and /gamerule soloLevelingDeathRules. New values apply to mobs as they spawn or reload; the modifier replacement means you will not get compounding stacks on old mobs.

nodes.title: Progression Presets
nodes.tagline: Standard, Fast, Custom - XP rate, Job Change level, gate access
nodes.summary: The Progression column of the world creation tab bundles XP Rate, the Job Change quest level, the Level Cap, and Gate Progress. Standard and Fast are fixed combinations; touching any individual control turns the preset to Custom.

facts.label: Standard (id 0)
facts.value: 1.0x XP, Job Change at level 40, ranked natural gates.

facts.label: Fast (id 1)
facts.value: 1.5x XP, Job Change at level 40, all natural gate ranks open.

facts.label: Custom (id 2)
facts.value: Keeps the individual progression settings you selected.

facts.label: XP Rate choices
facts.value: 1.0x, 1.5x, 2.0x in the UI (gamerule values 10/15/20).

facts.label: Job Change slider
facts.value: Level 20 to 100, default 40.

facts.label: Level Cap slider
facts.value: Unlimited (0) to 300 in steps of 10, default 150.

facts.label: Gate Progress
facts.value: Ranked (limits natural gates to your progression) or Open (every gate rank can appear).

sections.heading: The Level Cap
sections.body: The cap is the peak of the progression curve. Reaching it ends levelling and opens the return to the Cartenon Temple. Setting the slider all the way left selects Unlimited, which restores endless levelling with no ending trigger. Values above 300 set by command are treated as 300. Low caps are deliberately allowed - they are the practical way to reach the ending quickly.

sections.heading: Ranked versus Open gates
sections.body: With Ranked gates (the default), naturally spawning gates are limited to ranks that match the target player's Solo Leveling progression, so a fresh E-rank hunter does not get an S-rank gate on their doorstep. Open removes that limit and lets any rank spawn.

sections.heading: How the preset is detected
sections.body: The tab derives the shown preset from the actual rule values: XP 10 + Job Change 40 + Ranked gates reads as Standard; XP 15 + Job Change 40 + Open gates reads as Fast; anything else reads as Custom. The Level Cap is not part of preset detection - you can change it without leaving Standard or Fast.

nodes.title: Death Rules
nodes.tagline: What dying inside a Solo Leveling dungeon costs you
nodes.summary: The soloLevelingDeathRules gamerule controls what happens when you die inside a Solo Leveling dungeon dimension. It has three modes: Standard, Forgiving, and Harsh. Deaths outside mod dungeons always follow normal Minecraft rules.

facts.label: Standard (0, default)
facts.value: Vanilla inventory and experience loss.

facts.label: Forgiving (1)
facts.value: Keep your inventory and vanilla experience after a Solo Leveling dungeon death. Nothing drops on the ground.

facts.label: Harsh (2)
facts.value: Vanilla death rules, plus you lose 25% of your Solo Leveling XP and 10% of your gold.

facts.label: Where it applies
facts.value: Only in the mod's dungeon dimensions (dungeon instance dimensions and the Cartenon Temple). Overworld and other dimensions are untouched.

facts.label: Set by
facts.value: The Death Rules button in the Difficulty column at world creation, or /gamerule soloLevelingDeathRules <0|1|2>. Brutal difficulty selects Harsh automatically.

sections.heading: How Forgiving works
sections.body: The moment you die in a mod dungeon, the game snapshots your full inventory, selected hotbar slot, XP level, total XP, and XP progress. Your item drops and XP orb drops are cancelled, so nothing is left behind in the dungeon. When you respawn, the snapshot is restored exactly. This only protects deaths inside Solo Leveling dungeons - dying to a creeper in the overworld is still a normal death.

sections.heading: How Harsh works
sections.body: Harsh does not protect anything: you drop items and vanilla XP as usual. On top of that, your Solo Leveling XP is multiplied by 0.75 (a 25% loss) and your gold by 0.90 (a 10% loss). Your mod level itself is not directly reduced, but the XP loss can set you back toward earlier progress.

sections.heading: Practical advice
sections.body: If you play solo and hate corpse runs through dungeon mobs, Forgiving is the comfortable pick and costs you nothing mechanically. On Harsh, bank spare gold in purchases before risky runs, and remember that the /slr escape recovery command never awards dungeon progress but also does not count as a death.

nodes.title: Keybinds
nodes.tagline: Default keys for the System, skills, and abilities
nodes.summary: The mod registers 19 key mappings, most under the Solo Leveling Keybinds category in Options > Controls. All of them can be rebound. Keys only fire while no menu screen is open.

facts.label: N
facts.value: Open Panel. Opens your System panel. In a Dungeon Builder world it opens Builder Studio instead. Players without the System get a basic abilities screen.

facts.label: R
facts.value: Skill Cycle. Cycles the selected skill.

facts.label: Z
facts.value: Use the selected skill. Supports press-and-hold; the release time is sent too, so some skills care how long you held it.

facts.label: Right Mouse
facts.value: Sword Enhance. Hold-and-release, like Z.

facts.label: X
facts.value: Job Ability 1. Only responds in combat mode, or always if your class is Fighter.

facts.label: C
facts.value: Job Ability 2. Same combat-mode gate.

facts.label: V
facts.value: Job Ability 3. Same combat-mode gate.

facts.label: B
facts.value: Job Ability 4. Same combat-mode gate.

facts.label: Space
facts.value: Triple Jump. Sends your current momentum with the jump request.

facts.label: 1 through 8
facts.value: Skill hotbar slots 1-8. Press casts the slotted skill; hold-and-release is supported for charged skills.

facts.label: Tab
facts.value: Quest Info. Hold to view quest info; releasing clears the Demon King's Castle quest progress display.

facts.label: Left Mouse
facts.value: A mapping named Ddd registered under the Misc category. It has no action attached in the key mapping itself; leave it alone.

sections.heading: The combat-mode gate
sections.body: The four Job Ability keys (X, C, V, B) check a client-side condition before doing anything: your combat mode must be on, or your class must be Fighter. If you mash X and nothing happens, toggle combat mode first. The skill hotbar keys (1-8), Z, R, and the others do not have this client-side gate; the server decides whether the press does anything.

sections.heading: Hold-and-release keys
sections.body: Z, Right Mouse (Sword Enhance), X, and the 1-8 slots all report how long you held them when you let go. Charged or channeled skills read that duration. Quick taps and long holds can therefore do different things depending on the skill.

sections.heading: Rebinding and label quirks
sections.body: Everything lives under Solo Leveling Keybinds in the vanilla controls screen. Note two display quirks in the current language file: the slot-3 key is mislabeled as Ab 2 (same label as slot 2), and several keys share physical defaults with vanilla actions (Space, Tab, number keys, mouse buttons). The mod's mappings coexist with vanilla ones; rebind them if a conflict bothers you.

nodes.title: Player Commands
nodes.tagline: Recovery, party, and HUD commands anyone can run
nodes.summary: A small set of commands is available without operator permission. The most important ones are the recovery commands, which get you out of a broken or stuck dungeon safely instead of forcing a death.

facts.label: /slr help (or /slr recovery)
facts.value: Prints the recovery command list.

facts.label: /slr stuck
facts.value: Smart recovery: inside the Demon King's Castle it returns you to the current floor's entrance; in any other dungeon it leaves safely.

facts.label: /slr escape
facts.value: Emergency exit from your active dungeon. Dungeon progress is not awarded; you are returned safely to where you entered from.

facts.label: /slr dkc status
facts.value: Shows your current Demon King's Castle floor and whether you are inside the owned floor cell.

facts.label: /slr dkc unstuck
facts.value: Teleports you to the safe entrance of your current DKC floor. Encounter progress is preserved.

facts.label: /slr dkc leave
facts.value: Abandons the Demon King's Castle safely. Completed-floor progress is preserved.

facts.label: Recovery cooldown
facts.value: 10 seconds (200 ticks) shared across all recovery commands.

facts.label: /Party
facts.value: Shows your party. Subcommands: Create <name> [pass], Join <name> [pass], Leave, Members, Show. Note the capital P.

facts.label: /ToggleCustomHUD
facts.value: Toggles the mod's custom HUD on or off.

facts.label: /solodungeonstuck
facts.value: Older emergency escape. Returns you from a dungeon if an active recovery point exists.

facts.label: /dkcdebug
facts.value: Prints Demon King's Castle debug output for your position.

sections.heading: When to use which recovery command
sections.body: If you fell out of a dungeon's playable area, got sealed behind blocks, or a wave will not finish: run /slr stuck first. It picks the right behavior for where you are. Use /slr escape when you want out of a dungeon entirely and accept losing that run's progress. Inside the Demon King's Castle, /slr dkc unstuck keeps you on your floor and keeps your encounter progress, while /slr dkc leave abandons the attempt but keeps every floor you already completed.

sections.heading: Recovery is not a free teleport
sections.body: All recovery commands share a 10-second cooldown, /slr escape explicitly withholds dungeon rewards, and none of them work if you are not actually in a dungeon. They exist so a bug or a bad fall never traps your character, not as a travel tool.

sections.heading: Parties
sections.body: /Party Create <name> makes a party, with an optional password as a second argument. Others join with /Party Join <name> [pass]. /Party Members lists who is in it, /Party Leave exits, and /Party Show (or bare /Party) displays your current party. The same party system also has a GUI; the commands are a compatibility layer over the same server-side service.

nodes.title: Admin Commands
nodes.tagline: Operator tools: /slr player admin, /slrdungeon, structure spawners
nodes.summary: Operators get a deep /slr command tree for editing any player's progression, plus /slrdungeon for the datapack dungeon runtime and a set of structure placement commands. Permission levels vary: most /slr admin branches need level 3, /slrdungeon and /slnotify need level 2, and the raw structure spawners need level 4.

facts.label: /slr <players> ... (perm 3)
facts.value: Root for all per-player admin edits. <players> accepts selectors like @a.

facts.label: level <0-500>
facts.value: Sets the target's Solo Leveling level.

facts.label: class <name>
facts.value: Sets class: assassin, mage, fighter, tanker, healer, ranger, or random.

facts.label: rank <E|D|C|B|A|S>
facts.value: Sets Hunter rank directly.

facts.label: reset
facts.value: Full progression reset for the target.

facts.label: vessel ...
facts.value: select opens the vessel choice screen, reset clears it, ruler/monarch assign one directly (rulers: ashborn, thomas_andre, liu_zhigang, christopher_reed, go_gunhee; monarchs: sillad, baran, rakan, antares). The soloLevelingMonarchLimit gamerule still applies.

facts.label: dkc <floor 1-20>
facts.value: Queues fresh Demon King's Castle floor state for the target.

facts.label: gold Set|Add|reset
facts.value: Edits the target's gold.

facts.label: stats ...
facts.value: skillpoints/strength/vitality/agility/intelligence each take Set <n> and Add <n>; sense takes Set <0-100> only.

facts.label: shop set <slot 1-6> <item> / get <slot>
facts.value: Edits or reads the six System shop slots.

facts.label: rewards ...
facts.value: collect claims pending rewards; set <slot 1-3> preloads RandomItem, FullRecovery, SkillPoints <n>, Golds <n>, or Item <item>, each with an AutoCollect flag.

facts.label: OP ...
facts.value: DungeonBreak forces a dungeon break, TriggerPenaltyZone starts the penalty zone, FinishDaily completes the daily, TriggerDaily starts a fresh Daily Quest, TriggerJobchange resets and unlocks Job Change (overworld targets only).

facts.label: shadows ...
facts.value: add/remove <shadow> grants or removes a shadow soldier by id (tab-complete suggests valid ids); level <shadow|all> add/set <n> edits shadow levels up to 1,000,000.

facts.label: guild ...
facts.value: list all guilds; level <1-10> and xp <n> edit the target's guild; give hands out a Guild Computer; leave removes the target (disbands if owner); remove <player> kicks a member from the target owner's guild.

facts.label: generate dungeon <1-10> [theme]
facts.value: Generates a legacy procedural dungeon at the target. Themes: stone, ice, nether, desert, mossy, void, deepslate, prismarine.

facts.label: proceduraldungeon <rank> <theme> <complexity 1-10>
facts.value: Perm 3. Generates a ranked procedural dungeon (E-S) and teleports the target to its start.

facts.label: structure <set>
facts.value: Places every room template of a named dungeon set in a row for inspection (instance, kasaka, erank, cemetery, lab, large, kamish, dkc, kargalgan, igris, beru, ancientgolem, lush, random, cartenon, and more via tab-complete).

facts.label: /slr rift info (perm 3)
facts.value: Read-only Rift dimension diagnostics at your position: region, territory, radius, expected mob level.

facts.label: /slrdungeon (perm 2)
facts.value: Datapack dungeon runtime console. See the section below.

facts.label: /slnotify (perm 2)
facts.value: Tests the System notification overlay: title <text>, under <text>, both <title> | <under>. Supports & color codes.

facts.label: /soloresetportals, /soloresetstats (perm 3)
facts.value: Resets gate/portal state, and resets stats, respectively.

facts.label: spawn* commands (perm 4)
facts.value: spawnancientgolem, spawnberu, spawncemetery, spawndkc, spawnigris, spawninstance, spawnkargalganthrone, spawnlab, spawnlush, spawnrandom, spawnrandomlarge - each places that dungeon's structure at your position. Debug and map-making tools.

sections.heading: The /slr player tree
sections.body: Almost every admin edit follows the pattern /slr <players> <branch>. Examples: /slr @p level 80, /slr Steve class mage, /slr @a rank C, /slr Steve stats strength Set 200, /slr Steve gold Add 5000. The <players> argument requires permission level 3, so regular players cannot reach any of these branches. Selectors affect every matched player.

sections.heading: /slrdungeon - the datapack dungeon console
sections.body: Requires permission level 2. Subcommands: list (loaded dungeon definitions), issues (datapack validation messages), generate <namespace:id> [level <1-1000>] [seed <n>] confirm (builds the dungeon from a safe origin 64 blocks in front of you), instances / instance <uuid> / enter <uuid> / remove <uuid> confirm / prune (instance management), encounter reset <uuid> <key> confirm (recovers a stuck wave), portal <uuid> (repairs a return portal), and pool test <namespace:id> <level> (rolls a mob pool to check it resolves). Enter only works from the overworld so your return position can be saved. Remove deletes instance state and loaded tracked mobs but intentionally leaves generated blocks in place.

sections.heading: Vessel and shadow administration
sections.body: Vessel assignment respects the soloLevelingMonarchLimit gamerule, so on a server with the default limit of 1 you cannot hand the same Monarch to two players. Shadow ids for /slr <player> shadows are suggested by tab completion; the special target all in the level branch edits every shadow the player owns at once. Some vessel and shadow entries visible in tab completion belong to unreleased work-in-progress content; if an entry is rejected or behaves oddly, it is not finished.

nodes.title: Dungeon Builder
nodes.tagline: A dedicated world type for building and exporting your own dungeons
nodes.summary: The Dungeon Builder is a special world preset where you author custom dungeons: build rooms, mark them with five wands, wire up mob pools and encounters in the Builder Studio, then export a datapack. Exported dungeons can be opened with the Datapack Dungeon Gate Spawn Egg and valid ones also join the natural gate pool.

facts.label: How to start
facts.value: Create a new world and pick the Dungeon Builder world type. It is a void world with a 9x9 smooth stone platform at 0, 64, 0.

facts.label: On join
facts.value: You are put in Creative, the five architect wands are added to your inventory, a live checklist HUD appears on the right, and mod systems (daily quests, fatigue, gates, punishment) are switched off for that world.

facts.label: Open the Studio
facts.value: Press N (the Open Panel key) inside a builder world.

facts.label: Permissions
facts.value: The wands and /dungeonbuilder need operator level 2, or being the singleplayer world owner. All /dungeonbuilder commands only work inside a builder world.

facts.label: The five wands
facts.value: Surveyor (structure bounds, room bounds), Socket (corridor and stair doorways, required variants), Encounter (spawn points, trigger regions), Feature (player start, exit, return portal), Builder (studio, capture, status, preview, validate, undo, erase, export).

facts.label: Wand controls
facts.value: Right-click a block to use the current mode. Sneak + right-click air to cycle modes. Right-click air to inspect or run the mode.

facts.label: Studio tabs
facts.value: ROOMS, ANCHORS, POOLS, LAYOUT, SIMULATE, EXPORT, plus a Dungeons catalog for saved dungeon definitions.

facts.label: Export target
facts.value: A datapack written into the world's own datapacks folder. Export enables and reloads it automatically.

facts.label: Key limits
facts.value: Encounter levels 1-1000, room weight 1-10000, shell thickness 0-4 blocks, procedural exports 3-64 rooms.

facts.label: Testing
facts.value: Use the Datapack Dungeon Gate Spawn Egg and pick your dungeon in its screen. Operators can also use /slrdungeon generate in any world.

sections.heading: The workflow
sections.body: 1. ROOMS: create one module project per physical room, build the room, mark tight Structure Bounds and walkable Room Bounds with the Surveyor, then explicitly press Capture Room - block snapshots are never autosaved. 2. Sockets: mark doorway rectangles with the Socket Wand so the generator knows where rooms can connect; corridor sockets must face horizontally. 3. POOLS and ANCHORS: author weighted mob pools, then assign every generic spawn point a role (normal, elite, boss), a pool, and an encounter id. 4. LAYOUT: create a saved dungeon definition, include your rooms, set allowed ranks, room counts, and the protective shell, then press Apply. 5. SIMULATE a seed, then EXPORT: Validate, fix every blocking issue, and Export Pack.

sections.heading: Rooms are modules, not scenes
sections.body: The single most common mistake: one module project equals one physical room. Do not mark a start room, normal room, and boss room inside one project. Room roles are start, normal, corridor, junction, dead_end, treasure, stair, and boss. A minimal working dungeon is three modules - one START with a Player Start and Return Portal, one NORMAL with two sockets and a spawn point, one BOSS with an entrance socket and a boss spawn. /dungeonbuilder tutorial walks you through exactly this build in four steps.

sections.heading: Encounters and triggers
sections.body: Encounters spawn automatically when their room is entered unless you deliberately assign a Trigger Region to their encounter id, which delays the wave until a player enters that region. Spawn points are metadata, not saved entities - the actual mobs are rolled from the assigned pool at the dungeon's effective level when the dungeon runs. If you configure an encounter with a mob id instead of a pool id, export automatically creates the required one-mob pool.

sections.heading: Command reference
sections.body: /dungeonbuilder help and tutorial [1-4] explain the flow in game. project new <namespace> <name> <preset|module>, project select, project list, project reset confirm, project delete confirm, project role <role>. encounter list/select/configure <group> <pool> <min> <max>. settings rank <E-S|all>, settings ranks <min> <max>, settings pool normal|boss <id>, settings weight <1-10000>, settings shell <block> <0-4>. status, preview, validate, undo, export, and export procedural <name> <min_rooms> <max_rooms>. The Studio is the recommended path; the commands exist for automation and recovery.

sections.heading: From export to gameplay
sections.body: Export writes a datapack into that world's datapacks folder and reloads it, and tells you the saved path. Test immediately with the Datapack Dungeon Gate Spawn Egg, which lists every loaded datapack dungeon. Valid exported dungeons also enter the natural datapack-gate pool automatically, so they can appear as gates in a survival world that has the pack installed. Runtime diagnostics live in /slrdungeon: list, issues, pool test, generate, and instances.

nodes.title: Assassin
nodes.tagline: Daggers, teleports and openings you create yourself
nodes.summary: The Assassin fights up close with daggers, short teleports and concealment. Most of its abilities mark targets Exposed so your follow-up hits harder. Your class resource is Tempo: varied dagger actions fill a five-point meter that your finishers can cash in.

sections.heading: How Tempo works
sections.body: Tempo builds from varied dagger actions: dagger hits, thrown daggers, Ghost Step crossings, counters and ability hits. Repeating the exact same action within 0.3 seconds gives nothing, so mix your moves. At 5 points, the next Night Rend, Flash Cut, Mutilation detonation or Riposte consumes the whole bar for a 1.3x Perfect Cut multiplier and gives back one Ghost Step charge. Tempo builds for anyone who owns a spender ability, even if it was learned from a runestone.

sections.heading: Exposed and how to apply it
sections.body: Ghost Step through an enemy, land Night Rend, counter with Critical Attack, or ambush out of Veil. Exposed lasts 3 seconds from most sources (6 seconds from ambushes and from Night Rend as an Infiltrator) and makes your hits deal 15% more.

sections.heading: Getting abilities
sections.body: Your Hunter Evaluation assigns one of two styles. Each style is a fixed six-ability tree that unlocks one ability per Hunter rank, E through S. The grants are deterministic: two hunters with the same class, style and rank always have the same kit. Dagger Throw and Dagger Rush exist in the class but come from Ruler's Authority, not from rank progression. Cold Blood is a forbidden technique outside both trees.

sections.heading: Boss honesty
sections.body: Concealment never fully disables a boss. Stealth and Silent Domain make ordinary mobs lose you or chase a decoy, but anything tagged as a boss (or with 250+ max health) only drops its target for a moment and re-acquires on its own.

nodes.title: Infiltrator
nodes.tagline: Veil, isolation and strikes from unseen angles
nodes.summary: The Infiltrator is the concealment Assassin. You build an invisible Veil meter by moving while unwatched, then spend it all on one ambush strike that can hit for more than double damage. Your tree trades raw finishers for decoys, zones and an apex stealth state.

facts.value: Ghost Step, Stealth, Night Rend, Shadow Feint, Silent Domain, Zero Presence

facts.label: Veil meter
facts.value: 0-100; ambush ready at 60+

facts.label: Veil gain

facts.label: Ambush multiplier

sections.heading: Veil in practice
sections.body: Veil only builds while you are moving and no hostile mob within 24 blocks is targeting you or facing you with line of sight. Standing still earns nothing. At 60 or more Veil, your next dagger melee hit converts into an ambush: the whole meter is spent for a big multiplier, and the target is Exposed for 6 seconds. Dealing or taking any damage outside an ambush collapses the meter to zero, so commit to the opener. Veil grants no stealth or damage reduction by itself.

sections.heading: The tree
sections.body: Ghost Step (2 charges, 4.5s recharge each) blinks you 6 blocks; passing through an enemy Exposes it. Stealth (15s cooldown) drops a decoy and conceals you for 4-7 seconds scaling with Agility; recast to swap to the decoy's position; attacking from stealth deals 1.25x. Night Rend (8s cooldown) teleports you behind a target within 14 blocks for a 1.65x dagger opener. Shadow Feint (9s cooldown) leaves an attackable afterimage: if something hits it you are pulled to the attacker's flank with a 1.5x follow-up ready; recast to shatter it into a 3-second blind and slow; letting it expire refunds half the mana. Silent Domain (20s cooldown) places a 7-10 block dim zone for 8 seconds where up to 8 ordinary mobs keep losing their targets, with an upkeep drain on your mana. Zero Presence (60s cooldown, apex cost) is an 8-11 second state with 3 Vanish charges: each confirmed dagger hit spends one to reset your attack swing and Expose the target; it fills your Veil instantly but grants no immunity.

sections.heading: Playstyle
sections.body: Circle the fight, build Veil, open with an ambush or Night Rend, then keep Tempo up with varied actions. Your Exposed windows are twice as long as a Cutthroat's, so you have more room to convert setup into damage.

nodes.title: Cutthroat
nodes.tagline: Dagger tempo, critical windows and rapid finishes
nodes.summary: The Cutthroat is the aggression Assassin. Its tree is built around counters, multi-hit fans and the Mutilation mark-and-detonate loop. You stay in melee, cycle Tempo fast and cash in Perfect Cuts on finishers.

facts.value: Night Rend, Ghost Step, Critical Attack, Flash Cut, Mutilation, Dualwield

facts.value: 4s cooldown, up to 5 targets share one 0.9x budget

facts.label: Critical Attack
facts.value: 9s cooldown, 0.35s counter window; success evades the hit, Exposes the attacker and readies a 1.5x Riposte

facts.label: Mutilation
facts.value: Mark 7s, records up to 6 distinct cuts, detonates for power x (1 + 0.3 per cut)

sections.heading: The Mutilation loop
sections.body: Mark a target (needs line of sight within 18 blocks, 450 mana). For 7 seconds every distinct cut you land on it is recorded, up to 6 - Night Rend, Flash Cut, plain dagger hits and Dualwield follow-ups all count, but spamming the same action back-to-back does not. Recast to detonate early, or let the timer detonate for you. At 6 cuts the detonation hits for 2.8x your assassin power, and a full Tempo bar multiplies that again by 1.3.

sections.heading: Counters
sections.body: Critical Attack opens a very short window. If an enemy hits you inside it, the hit is cancelled, you teleport behind the attacker, it becomes Exposed, and your next dagger melee within 2 seconds deals 1.5x. Ghost Step also carries a brief evade window that Exposes whoever swung at you.

sections.heading: Dualwield
sections.body: With daggers in both hands, enter a 7-second stance. Each full-strength melee hit queues a follow-up strike, and every fourth hit crosses into nearby enemies. Your offhand dagger also adds 25% of your attack damage to every assassin ability while held.

sections.heading: Style bonus
sections.body: Night Rend's Exposed window is the short 3-second version for you - the style expects you to spend it immediately with the follow-up rather than sit on it.

nodes.title: Mage
nodes.tagline: Five elements, one Intelligence curve
nodes.summary: The Mage casts staged spells whose behaviour changes with your Intelligence, not just their numbers. Five styles exist and all five are enabled: Fire, Barrier, Arcane, Storm and Curse. Spells unlock one tier per Hunter rank, E through S.

facts.label: Spell unlocks

sections.heading: Output stages
sections.body: Every Mage style resolves an output stage from your effective Intelligence on the same ladder: below 30 is stage 1, then 30, 55, 80 and 110 step you up to stage 5. Stages change what a spell does - extra projectiles, new behaviours, bigger fields - and each style names its stages differently (Fire ends at Ultimate Weapon, Arcane at Transcendent, and so on).

sections.heading: Which style you get
sections.body: Your Hunter Evaluation draws one of the five styles from a non-repeating bag, so a reroll never immediately repeats what you just saw. Each style is a complete standalone spell set with its own resource or mark mechanic.

sections.heading: Costs scale with you
sections.body: Spell costs are a fraction of your maximum mana (which grows with Intelligence), multiplied by your stage: stage 1 pays the base and stage 5 pays 1.4x. Higher stages hit much harder than they cost extra.

nodes.title: Fire Mage
nodes.tagline: Scorch, explosive damage and area denial
nodes.summary: The Fire Mage stacks Scorch on enemies with fast weaving fire, then spends those stacks on lances and the Cremation execute. The capstone, Heavenfall, becomes the Day of Ruin at maximum output. Stages are named Ember, Blaze, Inferno, Cataclysm and Ultimate Weapon.

sections.heading: The Scorch economy
sections.body: Flame Weaving is your no-cost filler: a fast fire projectile whose every third hit marks the target with Scorch. Scorch stacks belong to you - another Fire Mage cannot spend yours. Inferno Lance consumes Scorch on whatever it pierces for bonus damage, and Cremation links every Scorched target near your aim and executes them in sequence.

sections.heading: Cremation pricing
sections.body: Cremation's mana cost is charged for the work it does: how many targets it links and how many stacks it detonates. More targets and deeper stacks cost more, but the cost never reads your predicted damage, so raising Intelligence never prices you out of your own finisher.

sections.heading: The rest of the kit
sections.body: Ignition Orb is a volatile projectile that collapses into an expanding blast. Flashfire turns you into living flame for a redirecting rush that burns what you pass through. Furnace Dominion builds a field that pulls, burns and finally erupts. Heavenfall calls descending fire; at Ultimate Weapon output it becomes the Day of Ruin.

nodes.title: Barrier Mage
nodes.tagline: Constructs, protection and battlefield control
nodes.summary: The Barrier Mage builds walls, prisons and wards, and marks enemies with Fracture using a fast bolt. Constructs and Fracture marks can be collapsed into one detonation. Stages are named Facet, Reinforced, Prismatic, Citadel and Absolute.

sections.heading: Fracture as a currency
sections.body: Fracture Bolt is a fast barrier shard that marks whatever it hits with Fracture. Sealing Prism consumes Fracture to hold targets in breakable prisons, and Resonant Collapse detonates your standing constructs and Fracture marks together in one controlled blast. Marks are per-caster.

sections.heading: Defence and control
sections.body: Prism Rampart raises a breakable wall that intercepts attacks and projectiles. Repulsion Frame drives a moving barrier through enemies to shove them where you want. Mirror Ward catches incoming pressure and returns it as capped retaliatory shards. Absolute Bastion, the S-rank capstone, constructs a fortress domain that shields allies and corrals enemies.

sections.heading: Control has limits
sections.body: Barrier control scales down against stronger targets: bosses resist hard control heavily and players partially, using a level-gap formula, so prisons hold trash solid but only inconvenience a raid boss.

nodes.title: Arcane Mage
nodes.tagline: Spatial formulas, mobility and precision
nodes.summary: The Arcane Mage shapes raw mana into formulas: correcting bolts, phase steps, gravity nodes and spatial cuts. Alternating different spells assembles a three-rune Arcane Formula. Stages are named Trace, Inscribed, Runic Array, Grand Formula and Transcendent.

sections.heading: The filler and the step
sections.body: Aether Bolt is condensed raw mana: a fast single trace at stage 1 that gains target correction, a pierce-and-ricochet, an inscribed triad and finally a constellation line as your stage rises. Vector Step rewrites your movement vector as a safe, collision-aware phase step; from stage 2 it leaves a recall anchor you can sneak-cast to return to, and at high stages it curves toward targets and leaves damaging afterimages.

sections.heading: Field tools
sections.body: Polarity Sphere creates a gravity node that pulls or repels bodies and loose projectiles - sneak to reverse its polarity. Runic Relay links two runes so later Arcane attacks emerge from the distant glyph, effectively letting you shoot around corners. Astral Arsenal keeps a ring of mana blades orbiting you that acquire targets on their own, or launch together when you recast.

sections.heading: Capstones
sections.body: Dimensional Rend cuts space with a long plane; sneak for a shorter, wider rupture, and higher stages add crossing cuts and a lingering spatial scar. Grand Formula: Convergence assembles a battlefield formula that gathers enemies, strikes its vertices and collapses the center - at Transcendent output a sky formula crushes the field against the ground array.

nodes.title: Storm Mage
nodes.tagline: Voltage, movement and controlled chain damage
nodes.summary: The Storm Mage marks enemies Conductive, routes lightning between them and banks Voltage from combat. At 100 Voltage your next eligible cast is Overcharged. Stages are Spark, Current, Surge, Tempest and Stormborn, with a sixth Sovereign Tempest stage that only a White Flame vessel transformation can reach.

sections.heading: Marks and routing
sections.body: Static Needle is the free-flowing filler: a precise bolt that marks enemies Conductive for 6 seconds. Lightning Rod privately designates one enemy as your routing root for 12 seconds. Chain Lightning routes a bounded chain through visible enemies - up to five unique targets at high stage - and prefers your marks and rod.

sections.heading: Overcharge
sections.body: Combat fills your Voltage meter. At 100 the next Static Needle, Thunderclap, Chain Lightning, Thunderhead or Skybreaker consumes it all for an Overcharged version: Thunderclap for example converts from a forward cone into a radial peel. Voltage drains if you stay out of combat.

sections.heading: The big casts
sections.body: Slipstream is a safe four-tick dash that can cleanse Slowness and harvest a nearby mark; stage 4 banks an extra dash charge. Thunderhead places a short-lived storm that delivers five to six scheduled strikes over seven seconds. Skybreaker is a telegraphed vertical finisher on a marked target or point that can fork into nearby Conductive enemies. Tempest Incarnate wears the storm for ten seconds: extra speed, accelerated Voltage, and every third cast produces a bounded echo.

sections.heading: The sixth stage
sections.body: The Sovereign Tempest stage is not reachable by Intelligence alone. It exists as a temporary bonus stage granted by a transformation - the White Flame Monarch vessel's spiritualization - and upgrades every spell's top behaviour while it lasts.

nodes.title: Curse Mage
nodes.tagline: Afflictions, decay and misfortune worked through others
nodes.summary: The Curse Mage splits casting in two: the curse wheel decides what lands, and delivery abilities decide how. Cooldowns belong to the curse, not the ability, and scale with how widely you spread it. Stages are Ill Omen, Malediction, Affliction, Anathema and Calamity.

sections.heading: Arm, then deliver
sections.body: Hold Curse Weave to open the wheel and release to arm a curse. Then pick a carrier: Hex Bolt spits it into one target at range, Malefic Burst detonates it across everything near your aim, Creeping Miasma leaves a lingering field that curses whatever walks in, and Vector of Ruin lets allies land your curse with their own hits. Culling detonates every curse you have placed nearby at once.

sections.heading: Cooldowns live on the curse
sections.body: When a curse lands, that curse goes on lockout - the ability does not. Spreading one curse over a crowd locks it out up to 2.5 times longer than a single-target cast, so wide delivery costs you rotation, not potency. This is why running several curses at once is safe to allow: each has its own timer.

sections.heading: The six curses
sections.body: Withering rots life away over time. Enfeeblement saps everything the target deals out. Leaden weighs targets down and makes them easy to throw around. Mana Rot corrodes the target's mana and feeds a share back to you. Blight leaps to the nearest uncursed enemy when its host dies. Doom marks an ending: if the mark survives its timer, it detonates.

sections.heading: Purification arms race
sections.body: A curse remembers the Intelligence stage it was cast at. A purifier can only strip a curse within one stage above their own - two stages of gap means the weaver was simply operating on a different level and the curse cannot be cleansed at all.

nodes.title: Fighter
nodes.tagline: Fists, swords or claws - pick how you break things
nodes.summary: The Fighter is the melee damage class with three enabled styles: Striker (fists and guard breaks), Swordsman (movement cuts) and Mutant (beast transformation). Its class passive is the Battle Gauge: landing hits fills a bar that bursts into Speed II and Strength II for six seconds.

sections.heading: Three resources, one class
sections.body: Each style has its own meter. Striker builds Impact stacks on the enemy it hits, Swordsman builds Sword Tempo from sword strikes, and Mutant builds a Feral meter from dealing and taking damage. The meters only exist while you own an ability that uses them, and all three retire automatically if you lose the kit.

sections.heading: Progression
sections.body: Your evaluation draws one of three styles, and each style is a fixed six-ability tree unlocked one ability per Hunter rank, E through S. A Fighter with no style keeps the classic sword kit.

sections.heading: Boss rules
sections.body: Knock-away finishers, spikes and launches do not move bosses (anything boss-tagged or with 250+ max health). Guard Break still lands on bosses but as Weakness rather than a slow.

nodes.title: Striker
nodes.tagline: Guard breaks, punch strings and close-range impact
nodes.summary: The Striker fights bare-knuckle. Its abilities stack Impact on whatever they hit; five stacks break the target's guard. The tree runs from Ground Slam up to Titan's Barrage, a twelve-strike apex combo.

sections.heading: Impact lives on the target
sections.body: Ground Slam, Cross Strike, Iron Knuckle, Breaker Combo, Meteor Fist and Titan's Barrage all add Impact to what they hit. The stacks are keyed to you, so another Striker cannot steal your guard progress. Fill five and the guard breaks.

Breaker Combo (12s cooldown) is an input-timed three-parter paying 25/30/45% of one budget; look down on the third input to spike the target into the ground instead of knocking it away. Missing a window ends the combo safely and you only pay for the steps you used.

sections.heading: Mobility and the capstone
sections.body: Meteor Fist (20s cooldown) leaps you up to 12 blocks to a point - it fails for free if there is no safe landing - and lands a direct impact worth 3 stacks plus a shockwave on up to 6 more enemies. Titan's Barrage locks one target within 6 blocks into twelve rising strikes and a finisher that breaks guard and launches anything that is not a boss.

nodes.title: Swordsman
nodes.tagline: Movement cuts, sword waves and precise finishers
nodes.summary: The Swordsman blends movement with blade work: dashes, projected sword waves and stance play. Sword hits build Sword Tempo, and a full bar empowers Radiant Execution, the style's precision line cut.

sections.heading: The classic kit

Sword Beam launches a slash-shaped energy wave that pierces up to 3 targets with falloff. Slash Fury is a directional sequence of 5 ordered slashes on one budget - you are slowed during it, not frozen. Sword Dance marks a target and flank-steps on each confirmed hit, up to 4 steps, ending early if no safe position exists. Sword of Light is a luminous stance that plants Light Seals on targets; the heavy input launches sealed enemies or spends the seals on a beam.

The first target takes the full budget, the second takes 45%, and anything below 30% health takes 15% more. A full Sword Tempo bar multiplies the whole cut by 1.3. It is deliberately tuned to sit under Titan's Barrage, not to replace it.

The bar drains a point every 1.5 seconds once you stop landing hits for 5 seconds, so keep the pressure up between finishers.

sections.heading: Feral in and out

Transformations spend Feral to enter, and keeping the meter above 60 cuts their mana upkeep by 40% - staying aggressive literally makes the form cheaper to hold. A beast form cannot overlap a vessel transformation.

sections.heading: The claws
sections.body: Claw Strikes (6s cooldown, cheap) is a three-swipe chain: each swipe hits up to 3 targets for a share of the budget and applies Rend. Look down on the last swipe to focus it into one target at 1.3x with double Rend. Predator Rush (20s cooldown) bounds you up to 16 blocks onto a target and mauls it - 1.3x if it already carries 3 Rend - and fails for free without a safe approach.

sections.heading: Hunter's senses
sections.body: Magical Eye (10s cooldown) outlines up to 8 enemies below 70% health within 10-16 blocks, scaling with Perception - your wounded-target radar. Beast Sense (15s cooldown) grants Speed II and jump assistance for 5-8 seconds scaling with Agility.

sections.heading: Why the two names
sections.body: The mod author presents this style as Mutant in reference material; the code and the in-game evaluation screen currently display it as Mutant. Same style, same tree.

nodes.title: Tanker

nodes.summary: The Tanker absorbs, delays and redirects damage. Its class passive is Iron Wall: taking and dealing Tanker hits builds stacks that shave a percentage off incoming damage. Two styles exist: Sentinel (shield and party protection) and Juggernaut (body mass and grapples).

sections.heading: Iron Wall
sections.body: Getting hit grants stacks, and Sentinel casts grant more (Taunt gives 1-3 based on targets, a perfect Reinforcement brace gives 2). At 10 stacks you shrug off 20% of PvE damage before anything else applies. Damage reduction from all Tanker sources is capped so you can never become unkillable: total custom reduction is limited per hit.

sections.heading: Two very different styles
sections.body: Sentinel is the shield-and-party tank: taunts, braces, delayed damage and a protection zone. Juggernaut shares nothing with it - no shields, just body mass, grapples, a giant form and ground-shattering finishers, all fed by its own Poise meter.

sections.heading: Honest anti-cheese
sections.body: Willpower strain - damage you delayed - cannot be erased by logging out, changing dimension or resetting your class. It settles, one way or another.

nodes.title: Sentinel
nodes.tagline: Shield control, threat and party protection
nodes.summary: The Sentinel is the classic protector. Taunt claims attention, Reinforcement rewards timed braces, Willpower delays damage as Strain you settle later, and Protection Mark spends a zone's integrity to shield allies. Costs are flat mana plus a percentage of your maximum.

sections.heading: Threat
sections.body: Taunt forces ordinary mobs onto you for 6 seconds and bosses for 2. Players cannot be mind-controlled - instead they get Challenged: for 3 seconds their damage against anyone who is not you is reduced. Casting it also grants 1-3 Iron Wall stacks depending on how many enemies you caught.

sections.heading: Reinforcement and the perfect brace
sections.body: Reinforcement opens a 0.6-second Perfect Brace window. Take a hit inside it and you convert into a 4-second Reinforced Stance with extra damage reduction and reduced knockback, plus 2 Iron Wall stacks. Brace against a telegraphed hit, not on reflex.

sections.heading: Willpower is a loan
sections.body: For 8 seconds, a share of the damage you retain is delayed as Strain instead of hurting you now: 50% against mobs, 40% against bosses, 30% in PvP, capped at 40/35/25% of your max health. When Willpower ends, the Strain settles back onto you in 4 pulses over 2 seconds. Landing Shield Bash during Willpower relieves up to 8% of your max health in Strain, once per activation. Strain survives logout and class changes - it always settles.

sections.heading: Protection Mark
sections.body: Deploys a 6-block zone for 12 seconds with an integrity pool equal to 75% of your maximum health. Allies inside take reduced damage (10-18% depending on the threat; you get a smaller share) and every prevented point drains integrity - boss damage drains it half again as fast. One mark per Sentinel; when the pool empties, the zone breaks.

sections.heading: The rest
sections.body: Shield Bash needs a shield in your offhand and solid ground: a short 3.6-block advance that strikes the first enemy in the path. Tank Leap jumps you 8 blocks forward and gathers up to 16 enemies at the landing point, slowing what it catches so you can establish position.

nodes.title: Juggernaut
nodes.tagline: Body mass, grapples and space denial
nodes.summary: The Juggernaut tanks without a shield. Holding ground under pressure builds Poise, which pays for Gigantification and discounts Mountain Breaker. Grapples pin ordinary enemies, drags collect crowds, and everything about the style rewards standing in the middle of the fight.

sections.heading: Poise
sections.body: Everything about holding ground feeds the meter: swinging, grappling, getting hit, resisting knockback. It bleeds 2 points every 2 seconds out of combat, so it is a fight-length resource, not a bank. Braced states (Iron Body or Gigantification) also cut knockback against you by 75%.

sections.heading: The control kit
sections.body: Heavy Blow (7s cooldown) is a slow armored swing with modest damage, heavy knockback and a slow. Seismic Grapple (15s) pins an ordinary target in place for 2 seconds - zero movement - while bosses and players are only slowed, never locked. Colossus Charge (21s) is a 1.2-second armored rush with Resistance III that drags every normal enemy it touches along the front, then flings the whole collection outward when it ends.

sections.heading: Iron Body timing
sections.body: Iron Body grants Resistance II for 4-8 seconds scaling with Vitality. Its first 0.6 seconds are a perfect window: a hit taken inside it deals 55% less and converts into 18 Poise. It is Reinforcement's cousin, tuned for a style with no shield.

sections.heading: Mountain Breaker
sections.body: A two-stage ground impact in a 6-block radius: an outward lift, then an inward collapse 0.8 seconds later that drags survivors toward the center and slows them. Having 40+ Poise discounts the apex mana cost by 35%, but Poise can never fully pay for it.

nodes.title: Healer
nodes.tagline: Intelligence-staged support - your style stays private
nodes.summary: The Healer keeps the party alive with abilities that grow new behaviours at Intelligence milestones, on the same 30/55/80/110 ladder Mages use. Two styles exist, Saint and Shepherd, but the game deliberately never shows anyone else which one you took.

facts.value: Heal Beam and Blessing Mark casts build stacks; at 5, a burst heals you and up to 5 wounded allies

facts.label: Ally rule

sections.heading: Stages change behaviour
sections.body: Every Healer ability resolves an output stage from your effective Intelligence, and stages add mechanics rather than just numbers. A stage-1 Heal Beam heals once; at stage 2 it adds regeneration, at 3 it cleanses, at 4 it chains to a second wounded ally, at 5 it leaves a regeneration mark. Read each ability's tooltip in-game - it shows your current stage.

sections.heading: Your style is private
sections.body: Saint and Shepherd decide your skill tree, but public identity surfaces - the association ID card, other players' inspection views - only ever say Healer. Advertising whether to expect single-target rescue or group coverage would tell enemies how to fight you before the fight starts. The style still fully applies internally.

sections.heading: Universal blessings
sections.body: Beyond the two style trees, Healers have a shared blessing set: Guardian Ward (layered resistance), Mana Font (restores 100-260 mana to allies by stage), Vitality Surge (max-health raise plus a heal into it) and Divine Favor (a capstone multi-buff reaching up to 6 allies at stage 5).

sections.heading: Cleansing curses
sections.body: Purification is the dedicated curse-breaker and spends its removal budget on curses before mundane debuffs. You can only strip a curse cast within one Intelligence stage above your own - a two-stage gap makes it untouchable.

nodes.title: Saint
nodes.tagline: Targeted rescue, cleansing and single-target recovery
nodes.summary: The Saint is the focused Healer: aim at one ally and pour output into them. Its capstone, Blessing Mark, banks a heal on someone and releases it automatically the moment they would drop below 30% health. Sneak to self-cast almost everything.

sections.heading: The rescue loop
sections.body: Heal Beam is your bread and butter on a 6-second cooldown. Purification strips 1-4 debuffs rising with stage, heals per removal from stage 3, and prioritises curses. Physical Buff and Haste Buff widen from one ally to two at stage 3, and every buff gets stronger tiers as your Intelligence climbs.

sections.heading: Overheal
sections.body: Healing an ally past full is not wasted - the excess is banked. Overheal converts 60% of your banked overhealing into an absorption shield, capped by stage, and at stage 3 shields a second nearby wounded ally too. It literally feeds on the healing you would otherwise have thrown away.

sections.heading: Blessing Mark
sections.body: The S-rank insurance policy. Mark an ally (or sneak to mark yourself): for 60 seconds a banked heal sits on them, and any hit that would drop them below 30% of max health triggers it instantly. At Divine output the mark holds two releases. Casting it and Heal Beam are also what build your Resonance passive.

nodes.title: Shepherd
nodes.tagline: Proximity healing, sanctuaries and group rescue
nodes.summary: The Shepherd heals by standing in the right place. Pulses, waves and fields hit everyone around you with no targeting needed, and Second Wind is a party-wide emergency button weighted by how hurt each ally is.

sections.heading: No targeting required
sections.body: Healing Pulse heals you and the most wounded allies within 6 blocks - at Divine output it pulses a second time. Purifying Wave cleanses and lightly heals everyone around you, including yourself. Sanctuary drops a stationary 6-block field that heals on its own timer for 10 seconds, adding stagger resistance inside at stage 4.

sections.heading: Mobility and escape
sections.body: Guardian Step dashes you to an ally and shields you both with absorption scaling by stage, healing both from stage 4 - and it fails for free when no safe landing exists. Camouflage drops threat, turns you translucent and clears you as a target from nearby mobs so you can reposition; at stage 4 it briefly conceals the most wounded nearby ally too.

sections.heading: Second Wind
sections.body: The party-wide emergency: every ally within 12 blocks gets a heal weighted by their missing health (base plus up to 35% of what they have lost), one cleanse, and damage resistance; stage 4 adds absorption on top. Sixty-second cooldown - spend it when the fight actually turns.

nodes.title: Ranger
nodes.tagline: Mana arrows, marks and the Focus gauge
nodes.summary: The Ranger fights at range with a bow and conjured mana ammunition. Arrow hits build the Focus gauge; a full gauge empowers your next shot or fuels the evolved Hyper Focus. Three styles are declared - Bowmaster, Saboteur, Gunslinger - but none are enabled yet, so the class currently plays one core kit.

sections.heading: Focus discipline
sections.body: Focus rewards a sniper's rhythm. It holds steady while you are drawing the bow, decays slowly while idle, decays four times faster while sprinting, and you lose 20 points when an attacker within 6 blocks hits you. Keep your distance and keep aiming.

sections.heading: The core kit
sections.body: Mana Quiver toggles conjured ammunition - no arrows needed - and gains Linear and Seeking arrow modes at B and A rank. Back Step retreats you safely on a charge system, fires a covering shot and accelerates your next draw. Hawkeye (26s cooldown) reveals hostiles in your aim cone for 18 seconds and grants night vision. Rapid Fire (9s cooldown) fires five controlled spectral arrows while you keep aiming. High Value Target (12s cooldown) marks one visible enemy within 64 blocks for extra damage and Focus; killing a marked mob refunds 200 mana and speeds up a Back Step charge. Sharpshooter fires a piercing Sunder Shot that exposes its target to your later arrows. Arrow Shower (20s cooldown, 1100 mana) rains five volleys onto an area up to 56 blocks away.

sections.heading: Evolutions
sections.body: Owning the full core kit evolves two abilities. Sharpshooter becomes Typhoon Shot: a harder-hitting pierce that detonates a windburst on first impact. Hyper Focus becomes Fivefold Execution: consume a full 100-Focus gauge to manifest five rapid precision arrows within ten seconds (48s cooldown). Without the full kit, Hyper Focus is an 8-second state that doubles Focus gain and accelerates arrow charging.

nodes.title: The System
nodes.tagline: The invisible administrator that turns you into a Player
nodes.summary: The System is the mod's core progression engine. Once you have it, kills grant XP, XP grants levels, levels grant stats and skill points, and quests and rewards start arriving. You do not start with it - you have to earn it by dying in the right place.

facts.label: How you get it
facts.value: Accept the awakening offer in the Cartenon Temple (the only code path that grants it)

facts.label: What it runs
facts.value: XP and levels, stat growth, skill points, daily quests, urgent quests, the System Rewards inbox

facts.label: Per level
facts.value: +1 to every stat and +3 skill points

facts.label: End state
facts.value: At the level cap you can release the System at the Statue of God; it then stops issuing XP, quests and rewards forever

facts.label: Reward inbox types
facts.value: Full Recovery, Skill Points, System Golds, XP, specific items, Random Item box

sections.heading: Getting the System
sections.body: You do not begin the game as a Player. Clear the boss of a ranked dungeon (D, C, B, A, S or the snow dungeon) while nobody in your party has the System yet. A hidden gate appears with the message 'A strange gate has appeared.' Step through it into the Cartenon Temple. Inside, the first hit that would kill you is cancelled and the System offers you a choice: accept and become a Player, or decline and die. Accepting fully heals you, grants the System, and returns you to the overworld. Declining is recorded permanently - the gate will not respond to you again. Story Mode reaches the same choice through a scripted prologue instead.

sections.heading: What changes once you have it
sections.body: Kills on eligible mobs now grant System XP. Levels grant +1 to every stat and +3 skill points each. A Daily Quest is assigned once per Minecraft day. Boss first-kills, urgent quests and quest completions push rewards into your System Rewards inbox, where you collect them manually. Full Recovery rewards restore health, mana and fatigue in one click.

sections.heading: The System can end
sections.body: The System is never destroyed, but at the very end of the run you can release it. After you reach the level cap and defeat the Statue of God in the Cartenon finale, the System keeps running with nobody at the controls: no more daily quests, no more XP from kills, no more reward payouts. Everything you already earned - stats, abilities, shadows, the shop - keeps working exactly as before. Releasing is permanent.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: Evaluation at a Hunter Rank Evaluator is separate from the System - anyone can be evaluated, with or without it. Creative mode players cast abilities for free but do not progress daily objectives.

nodes.title: Hunter Evaluation
nodes.tagline: Place your hand on the crystal and learn what you are
nodes.summary: Right-click a Hunter Rank Evaluator block to run the evaluation ceremony. It rolls your rank, reveals your class and style, and pays out a one-time awakening stat package. Rank is never rerollable; class is, once per draw, until you accept.

facts.label: Station
facts.value: Hunter Rank Evaluator block, right-click; stay within 8 blocks or the session pauses

facts.label: Rank roll
facts.value: 1-100 roll against the world's rank odds gamerules (defaults E 25% / D 25% / C 25% / B 12% / A 10% / S 3%)

facts.label: Rank reroll
facts.value: Never. Only class and style can be rerolled, and only during your first evaluation

facts.label: Class reroll
facts.value: Shuffle-bag draw: never the same class twice in a row, all six appear before any repeat

facts.label: Result rank
facts.value: max(rolled rank, previous certified rank, level floor); a vessel always measures S

facts.label: Reminder
facts.value: Unclassified players get an on-screen reminder at level 18 and again at level 20

sections.heading: The ceremony
sections.body: The crystal boots, you hold contact, it scans, then reveals class, style (for classes that have styles), and finally rank. An S-Rank reveal deliberately runs longer: the evaluator reports a measurement error before the real result resolves, with the wither-spawn sound. Walking more than 8 blocks away pauses the session; it resumes when you come back. At the decision step you can accept, reroll your class, or reroll your style. Accepting commits everything.

sections.heading: What accepting pays out (first evaluation only)
sections.body: Your class, style and rank are written to your Hunter profile, and a one-time awakening package is applied: a stat spread that scales with rank squared (times 1.25), weighted by class - an Assassin's package leans Agility and Sense, a Tanker's leans Vitality. Mage, Healer and Ranger use fixed Intelligence tables per rank instead (a Mage at S gets 120 base Intelligence before the multiplier). Ranks E through B get a further 15% rounding boost on all five stats. You also receive a class starter pack item, your class's base abilities, and a Hunter ID card bound to you. This package can never be applied twice.

sections.heading: Re-evaluation
sections.body: Visit the evaluator again after leveling and it certifies your current rank onto your Hunter ID. Re-evaluation only ever promotes - your certified rank can never go down. If your level has crossed a rank floor (D at 15, C at 30, B at 50, A at 75, S at 100), the new certification reflects it.

sections.heading: How the odds gamerules work
sections.body: The six gamerules soloLevelingRankOddsE through soloLevelingRankOddsS hold raw weights, not literal percentages. They are normalized proportionally: weights of 25/25/25/12/12/11 total 110, so the S weight of 11 yields a 10% chance. A rank with weight 0 can never be drawn.

nodes.summary: E is the lowest hunter rank and the default result for a low roll. It still counts: even E-Rank gets the first ability of its class tree and the full awakening stat package at its smallest scale.

sections.heading: Three ways in

sections.heading: The reveal

If you hear the wither, congratulations.

sections.heading: What it is worth
sections.body: The S awakening package is the largest in the game (rank-squared scaling: 36 x 1.25 = 45 per class weight unit; a Mage's fixed Intelligence table gives 120 base). S-scale gates and dungeons become your matched tier. There is nothing above it - past this, progression is levels, the cap, and the Cartenon finale.

nodes.title: Levels and XP
nodes.tagline: 16L + 8 per level, 8N squared to the top
nodes.summary: System XP comes from killing the mod's mobs. The cost of each level grows linearly, so total XP grows with the square of your level. The default cap is 150, and reaching it opens the ending.

facts.value: XP to advance out of level L = L x 16 + 8 (level 0 to 1 costs 8, level 100 to 101 costs 1608)

facts.label: Cumulative
facts.value: Total XP to reach level N = 8 x N squared (level 150 = 180,000 XP total)

facts.label: Level cap
facts.value: Gamerule soloLevelingLevelCap, default 150, slider max 300, 0 = unlimited

facts.label: Per level
facts.value: +1 Strength, Vitality, Agility, Sense, Intelligence; +3 skill points; fatigue reset to 0

facts.label: Difficulty multiplier
facts.value: Easy/Peaceful x1, Normal x0.75, Hard x0.5

facts.label: XP gamerule
facts.value: soloLevelingXPMultiplier default 10 = x1.0 (the value is divided by 10)

sections.heading: Where XP comes from
sections.body: Only System Players earn XP, and by default (gamerule soloDungeonProgressionOnly = true) only the mod's own mobs and dungeon-spawned mobs pay out. Sample base values: goblins 3, Steel Fang Wolf 5, Orc 25, High Orc 40; bosses range from Ancient Samurai 600 and Goblin King 900 through Igris 3000, Baruka 5000, Beru 10000 and Kamish 20000. Runtime dungeon mobs pay by their level and role (a dungeon boss pays at least 25, scaling at 2 per level). Kills made by your shadows, tamed pets and projectiles credit you. Turning the dungeon-only gamerule off makes everything else worth 1 base XP. Quest rewards pay their advertised XP with no multipliers applied.

sections.heading: Leveling up
sections.body: The level-up check runs continuously: whenever your banked XP covers the next level's cost it is spent, and multiple levels can pop at once. Every level grants +1 to all five stats and +3 skill points, wipes your fatigue to zero, and gives a short burst of regeneration, saturation and absorption. If your new level crosses a rank floor (15/30/50/75/100), your Hunter Rank is promoted on the spot with a RANK UP banner - once you have had your first evaluation.

sections.heading: The cap and the peak
sections.body: The default cap is level 150. XP earned past the cap is banked, not discarded - raising the cap or setting it to 0 (unlimited) later resumes exactly where you were. Hitting the cap fires a one-time message: 'THE PEAK - There is nothing left to climb. Return to where it began.' That is your cue: the Cartenon finale summons is now available.

sections.heading: Practical notes
sections.body: Harder difficulties pay LESS System XP, not more (Normal x0.75, Hard x0.5) - the mobs are already harder. Stronger leveled mobs pay up to x3 via a multiplier based on their stat scaling. After you release the System at the end of the run, kills stop paying XP entirely.

nodes.title: Strength
nodes.tagline: Your attack damage, straight up
nodes.summary: Strength sets your base attack damage. Every point adds a fixed slice of melee power, and many class abilities scale on it too.

facts.label: Formula
facts.value: Base attack damage = 1 + 0.075 x effective Strength

facts.label: Growth
facts.value: +1 per level; buy more at 1 skill point per point

facts.label: Cap
facts.value: None

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Your attack damage attribute is recomputed every tick from your effective Strength (base stat plus any temporary buffs). At 100 Strength your bare-hand base damage is 8.5; weapons add on top. Class abilities that scale physically read the same effective Strength value.

sections.heading: Getting more
sections.body: Every level gives +1 automatically. Skill points buy +1 per point spent. Class awakening packages weight Strength for Fighter (x4 of the rank curve) and Tanker (x2), and every rank E-B evaluation adds a 15% rounding boost.

nodes.title: Vitality
nodes.tagline: Health and hide in one stat
nodes.summary: Vitality raises your maximum health and gives you innate armor. It is the survival stat for every class, and the core stat for Tankers and Healers.

facts.value: 20 + 0.5 x Vitality

facts.label: Innate armor

facts.label: Growth

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Every 2 points of Vitality add one full heart of maximum health, and roughly every 17 points add one armor point on top of whatever you wear. 100 Vitality means 70 max health (35 hearts) and 6 innate armor.

sections.heading: Getting more
sections.body: +1 per level automatically, +1 per skill point spent. The awakening package weights Vitality hardest for Healers (x5) and Tankers (x4), and Rangers get x4 as well.

nodes.summary: Agility makes you faster while sprinting and swimming, lets you step up taller blocks, and at 70+ removes fall damage entirely.

facts.label: Swim speed
