sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The speed bonus only applies while sprinting - walking speed is unchanged. Step height upgrades in bands: at 30 Agility you walk up full blocks without jumping, at 50 you clear fences, at 100 you clear two-block ledges. From 70 Agility your fall distance is zeroed every airborne tick, so falls of any height are free.

sections.heading: Getting more
sections.body: +1 per level, +1 per skill point. Assassins get the heaviest Agility weighting at awakening (x5 of the rank curve), with Rangers at x3. The stat is stored internally as 'Speed' - same thing, the panel calls it Agility.

nodes.title: Sense
nodes.tagline: Dodge chance and a sixth sense for threats
nodes.summary: Sense gives you a random chance to fully dodge attacks with a sidestep teleport, and passively highlights nearby hostiles through walls. It is the only stat with an investment cap.

facts.label: Dodge chance
facts.value: Sense / 2000 per eligible hit (5% at 100) against melee, mob projectiles and magic

facts.label: Dodge effect
facts.value: The hit is cancelled, 'Rare Dodge!' flashes, and you teleport one block sideways

facts.label: Threat sense
facts.value: Each tick, a Sense/20000 chance to highlight nearby hostiles through walls, radius = Sense/2 blocks

facts.label: Investment cap
facts.value: 100 - the plus button stops there and never overcharges you

facts.label: Growth
facts.value: +1 per level; buy more at 1 skill point per point until 100

sections.heading: The dodge
sections.body: When a player attack, mob attack, mob projectile or magic damage source hits you, the game rolls against Sense/2000. On success the damage event is cancelled outright and you are displaced one block in a random horizontal direction. At the 100-point investment cap that is a 5% full dodge on most combat damage. Awakening stat packages can push Sense past 100 (a Ranger's S-rank package alone grants 180), and the dodge formula keeps scaling.

sections.heading: The sixth sense
sections.body: Passively, roughly every so often (chance Sense/20000 per tick, then a cooldown), the nearest hostile entities within Sense/2 blocks get a glowing outline you can see through walls, with a faint sculk click. Tamed and allied entities are never highlighted.

sections.heading: Getting more
sections.body: +1 per level, +1 per skill point, hard stop at 100 for purchases. Assassins (x4) and Rangers (x4) get the biggest awakening weights.

nodes.title: Intelligence
nodes.tagline: Your mana pool and how fast it refills
nodes.summary: Intelligence sets your maximum mana and your passive mana regeneration. Every ability cost in the mod is priced against the Intelligence-derived pool, so the stat also quietly defines what you can afford to cast.

facts.label: Max mana
facts.value: 1000 + 100 x effective Intelligence

facts.label: Regen
facts.value: +Intelligence/10 mana per tick on top of your base regen, whenever below max

facts.label: Cost model
facts.value: Ability costs = max(flat floor, pool x band fraction), so they scale with your pool

facts.label: Growth
facts.value: +1 per level; buy more at 1 skill point per point

facts.label: Caster tables
facts.value: Mage/Healer/Ranger awakening grants fixed INT by rank (Mage: 3/13/30/53/83/120 base for E-S)

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Your mana bar is 1000 plus 100 per point of effective Intelligence; a 100-INT caster has an 11,000 pool. Regeneration adds INT/10 mana every tick (a 100-INT caster regains 200 mana per second) - but wearing Shadow Armor or Goliath Armor suppresses passive regen entirely. Ability costs are bands expressed as fractions of the pool with flat floors, so low-INT physical classes pay predictable flat costs while casters' costs scale with their pool.

sections.heading: Flat mana grants
sections.body: Some endgame rewards (the Black Heart from the Cartenon finale) add a flat reservoir on top of the INT pool. Costs are deliberately never priced against those grants - only against the Intelligence-derived pool - so a 100,000-mana reward makes you richer without making anything more expensive.

sections.heading: Getting more
sections.body: +1 per level, +1 per skill point. Mage, Healer and Ranger awakenings use fixed per-rank Intelligence tables instead of the generic curve, multiplied by 1.25. Creative mode casts everything free regardless.

nodes.title: Fatigue
nodes.tagline: Push too hard and your body pushes back
nodes.summary: Fatigue accumulates from taking hits, blocking and jumping. At 75 (displayed) you slow down; at 100 you can barely move. Sleep it off, level up, or drink a fatigue potion.

facts.label: Gamerule
facts.value: soloFatigue, default on; survival mode only

facts.label: Display
facts.value: The HUD shows raw fatigue divided by 10 (FTG: 0-100+)

facts.label: Gain
facts.value: +0.2 shown per damage hit (max once per second), +0.5 per shield block, +0.1 per jump

facts.label: At 75 shown
facts.value: Slowness II and Mining Fatigue II

facts.label: At 100 shown
facts.value: Slowness XI, Weakness XI, Mining Fatigue VI - effectively stopped

facts.label: Recovery
facts.value: Sleeping drains it rapidly; level-up and Full Recovery reset it to 0; potions remove 10/50/100 shown

sections.heading: How it builds
sections.body: Most incoming damage adds fatigue (2 raw, at most once per second), except environmental sources like fire, lava, cactus, suffocation and bleeding, which are free. Blocking with a shield costs 5 raw per block, and every jump costs 1 raw. Only survival-mode players accumulate it.

sections.heading: The two thresholds
sections.body: Between 75 and 99 displayed you fight with Slowness II and Mining Fatigue II - annoying but workable. At 100 displayed the debuffs jump to Slowness XI and Weakness XI: you effectively cannot fight or flee. Do not let it get there mid-dungeon.

sections.heading: Clearing it
sections.body: Sleep is free: fatigue drains 5 raw per tick while you are actually in bed, so even a moment asleep clears a lot. Leveling up resets it to zero outright, as does any Full Recovery reward (daily quests hand these out). The shop sells three fatigue potion sizes removing 10, 50 and 100 displayed points.

nodes.title: Skill Points
nodes.tagline: One point, one stat, no waste
nodes.summary: Skill points are the currency you spend on stats. The exchange rate is exactly 1 point per +1 stat. They come from levels, dailies, urgent quests and boss first-kills.

facts.label: Exchange rate
facts.value: 1 skill point = +1 to a stat of your choice (Sense stops at 100)

facts.label: Secret Quest
facts.value: +6 on top of the daily's +3 (9 total)

facts.label: Urgent quests
facts.value: +2 to +4, random

facts.label: Boss first kills
facts.value: +3 to +10 by danger tier, once per boss ever

sections.heading: Spending
sections.body: Open your stat panel and press the plus button on a stat. You can configure an investment size; the game clamps it to what you can afford and only charges for whole attributes actually granted - a capped Sense press can never bill you for points it refused to spend. Points never expire.

sections.heading: Boss bounty table
sections.body: First kills pay by tier: Goblin King and Gem Golem 3, Ancient Golem 4, Fanged Kasaka and Futuristic Golem 5, Blood-Red Commander Igris 6, Baruka 8, Beru the Ant King 9, Kamish 10. Each is once per player, forever, and arrives through the System Rewards inbox alongside a Full Recovery and other loot.

sections.heading: Scarcity is the design
sections.body: The exchange rate used to be worse-than-1:1; it is now exactly 1:1 and the balance lever moved to how many points exist. Your awakening stat package was scaled up 25% to compensate. If you want raw stats fast, the daily quest is 3 guaranteed points a day before you swing a sword at a boss.

nodes.title: Daily Quest
nodes.tagline: Mine, fight, run - every day, on a 20-minute clock
nodes.summary: Once per Minecraft day the System assigns three objectives: mine 32 eligible blocks, earn 8 threat points from hostile kills, and travel 500 blocks on foot. Twenty minutes, or the Penalty Zone.

facts.label: Gamerule
facts.value: soloDailyQuest, default on; assigned once per Minecraft day (overworld clock)

facts.label: Timer
facts.value: 20 minutes, with warnings at 5 minutes and 1 minute left

facts.label: Mining
facts.value: 32 blocks: stone families, ores, netherrack, basalt, end stone, mana crystal deposits - correct tool required, each block position counts once

facts.label: Combat
facts.value: 8 threat points: normal hostile 1, elite 3, miniboss 4, boss 8; waived entirely on Peaceful

facts.label: Travel
facts.value: 500 blocks on foot - riding, flying, elytra and swimming do not count

facts.label: Rewards
facts.value: Full Recovery + 3 skill points + a random item box, via the System Rewards inbox

sections.heading: The objectives in practice
sections.body: Mining counts only blocks in the daily-mineable tag broken with the right tool, and remembers every position - place-and-break loops do nothing. Threat points come from genuine hostiles: your own shadows, tamed animals and other players' pets never count as targets, but kills MADE BY your shadows, pets and projectiles credit you. Distance is measured per tick on foot with a 2.5 blocks-per-tick sanity cap, so teleports and mounts are ignored. Creative and spectator progress does not count.

sections.heading: Guaranteed combat fallback
sections.body: If no hostiles are around, spawn a System Training Bot from the training menu. Killing your own bot is worth a flat 8 threat points - the whole combat objective in one kill. Only your own bot counts; someone else's bot or a spawn-egg bot does not.

sections.heading: Failure and the Penalty Zone
sections.body: When the timer expires, the quest fails. With gamerule soloPunishment on (default) - and only until you finish the Job Change quest - you are teleported to the Penalty Zone: survive 120 seconds. Giant centipedes spawn at 110, 90 and 70 seconds remaining. Survive and you are returned exactly where you were, with a 'SURVIVED!' banner. There is no XP penalty; you just try again tomorrow.

sections.heading: Fine print
sections.body: The quest only exists while somebody is running the System - after you release it in the finale, dailies stop forever. If world difficulty flips to Peaceful mid-quest, the combat objective is waived and stays waived for that quest.

nodes.title: Secret Quest
nodes.tagline: The daily that was never really a daily
nodes.summary: From level 30, your Daily Quest is silently flagged. Overshoot any objective past its normal target and it reveals itself as a Secret Quest with doubled goals - and a key to the Demon King's Castle at the end.

facts.label: Trigger
facts.value: Level 30+, Demon King's Castle not yet unlocked - then every daily is secretly flagged

facts.label: Reveal
facts.value: Push any objective past its normal target (33rd block, 9th threat point, 501st block of travel)

facts.label: Doubled targets
facts.value: 64 blocks mined, 16 threat points, 1000 blocks travelled

facts.label: Extra rewards
facts.value: A second Full Recovery, +6 more skill points (9 total), and the Demon King's Castle Key

facts.label: Unlocks
facts.value: The Demon King's Castle questline

facts.label: One-time
facts.value: Once the castle is unlocked, the Secret Quest never appears again

sections.heading: How it reveals
sections.body: The flag is invisible. Your daily looks normal until you exceed a normal target - at that instant the banner flips: 'Daily Quest turned into Secret Quest. Complete the hidden requirements.' All three targets double. If you finish the daily exactly at its normal targets without overshooting, the completion event still fires as a secret completion, because the quest was secret all along.

sections.heading: Worth chasing
sections.body: Completion stacks the normal daily rewards (Full Recovery, 3 skill points, item box) with the secret bonus: another Full Recovery, 6 more skill points, and the Demon King's Castle Key - the red key item that opens the mod's 20-floor castle climb. It also permanently unlocks the castle questline on your character.

sections.heading: If you fail
sections.body: Failing a daily while you are still eligible keeps the secret pending - it will be waiting inside a future daily. The window only closes when the Demon King's Castle is unlocked.

nodes.title: Cartenon Temple
nodes.tagline: Where the System begins, and where it ends
nodes.summary: A hidden instanced dimension behind a gate that only appears for hunters without the System. Dying inside triggers the awakening choice. At the level cap, the temple calls you back for the finale against the Statue of God.

facts.label: Dimension
facts.value: sololeveling:cartenon_temple, instanced per party on a 512-block grid

facts.label: Discovery
facts.value: Clear a D/C/B/A/S/snow dungeon boss with no System holders in the party - a hidden gate spawns

facts.label: First visit
facts.value: A lethal hit is cancelled and becomes the awakening choice: accept the System, or decline and die

facts.label: Decline
facts.value: Recorded permanently - the gate never responds to you again

facts.label: Finale trigger
facts.value: Reach the level cap, receive 'The Way Back' quest, kneel (hold sneak on the ground for 2 seconds)

facts.label: Finale reward
facts.value: Shadow Monarch job: the Black Heart (+100,000 flat max mana, unlimited shadow storage); anyone else: True Vessel Awakening

sections.heading: The first visit
sections.body: The hidden gate appears only when a dungeon boss falls to a party in which nobody has the System and nobody has already made their choice. It admits only the participants. Inside the temple, you cannot die: any hit that would kill you is zeroed, you are frozen in place, and the System makes its offer. Accept, and you become a Player - full heal, teleport to the overworld, 'You have become a Player.' Decline, and after a few frozen seconds you die, and the System writes your answer down for good.

sections.heading: The Way Back
sections.body: Reaching the level cap (default 150) fires 'THE PEAK' and, shortly after, an urgent quest titled The Way Back: 'Kneel to open the way to the Cartenon Temple.' Hold sneak while standing on the ground for two full seconds - deliberately long enough that it is never accidental. A one-use return gate opens beside you. It closes behind you.

sections.heading: The finale
sections.body: The Architect - the voice that built the System - speaks through System popups. Then every posed statue in the temple wakes at once. Then the Statue of God itself: heavy melee, plus a telegraphed eye beam (25-tick warning marker, 45 damage in a 3.5-block column, on a 5.5-second cooldown - stand in the circle and you deserve it). There is no dialog box at the end. Killing the Statue of God IS the decision.

sections.heading: The release
sections.body: The Architect concedes, and the System is released: it keeps running with nobody at the controls. No more quests, XP, levels or reward payouts - ever - but every stat, ability, shadow and item you earned keeps working. Shadow Monarchs inherit the Black Heart: a flat 100,000 bonus mana that never inflates ability costs, and no ceiling on shadow storage. Every other path gets the True Vessel Awakening. Then the temple puts you out, and closes: it has nothing left to measure.

facts.label: Your start

facts.label: Your party

sections.heading: The arc
sections.body: You spawn inside the Ancient Golem dungeon with a six-hunter NPC team. Clear it together. The boss falls, and instead of a way out, a strange gate appears. Beyond it: the Cartenon Temple, and the Statue of God. The script runs the scenes the mod is named for - the laser executions, the statues waking, the hunt - and your party does not make it. The prologue's stages are saved server-side, so relogging or dying resumes where the script left off.

sections.heading: The one death that matters
sections.body: In a normal Cartenon run, any lethal hit can trigger the awakening. In Story Mode the rules are stricter: only the Statue of God itself, after the party hunt is over, personally landing the killing blow on you, can trigger the choice. You cannot skip to the ending by jumping in lava. Accept the System and the prologue completes; the world then behaves like any other.

sections.heading: Should you turn it on
sections.body: Turn it on for a new world if you want the mod's opening delivered as an experience instead of a mechanic. Leave it off on multiplayer servers where the first login claiming a one-time solo prologue would be awkward - only the owner gets the scripted path; everyone else awakens through the normal hidden-gate route.

sections.heading: What a vessel is
sections.body: When you finish the Job Change Quest you choose one Monarch or Ruler to become the vessel of. That choice writes your job id and identity onto your character and unlocks that vessel's skill tree. Skills then unlock automatically as your System level rises; the server re-checks every unlock condition itself, so commands or stale client data cannot equip a skill early.

sections.heading: Rulers vs Monarchs
sections.body: Mechanically the split matters in two ways. First, every Ruler vessel receives Ruler's Authority (a telekinesis ability) the moment it is assigned, and receives its Spiritual Body Manifestation immediately rather than at level 120. Second, Monarch vessels get their spiritual body as a level 120 capstone instead. Note a quirk: Ashborn, the Shadow Monarch vessel, is typed as a Ruler in code, so it also receives Ruler's Authority at selection.

sections.heading: The server limit
sections.body: Vessel ownership is stored per world (saved data 'sololeveling_vessel_claims'). By default only one player can hold each vessel identity at a time. If someone already claimed the vessel you want, the selection screen tells you it reached the server limit. Ownership is released if that player's vessel is reset. Existing owners are grandfathered: lowering the gamerule never deletes a job someone already earned.

sections.heading: Ruler's Authority
sections.body: One key does everything: tap for a quick push, hold to grab an entity and move it with your camera, scroll to adjust hold distance (3 to 14 blocks, up to 22 with full Authority), release to throw, sneak-release to slam. Bosses resist being lifted; against them the hold becomes a pressure effect instead of full control.

sections.heading: Changing vessels
sections.body: The quest completes once. There is no player-facing way to swap vessels afterwards; only server operators can reset a player's vessel status or assign a different one, and a reset releases the world claim so the vessel opens up again.

sections.heading: What is open
sections.body:
All five Monarch vessels are selectable: Ashborn, Sillad, Baran, Rakan and Antares.

Two of the five Ruler vessels are selectable — the Adamant Fragment (Thomas Andre) and the Sharpest Fragment (Liu Zhigang). The Blazing, Silent and Brightest Fragments are marked **work in progress** on the selection screen and cannot be taken yet.

A world can also cap how many players hold the same vessel, which is why one may show as claimed even when it is finished.

sections.heading: Unlocking
sections.body: Once you are a System player and reach the unlock level while in the Overworld, the quest unlocks on its own with a 'QUEST UNLOCKED - Job Change Quest' popup. You do not need an item; the check runs continuously.

sections.heading: The Igris dungeon
sections.body: Entering the quest teleports you into a dedicated dungeon dimension and spawns the Igris encounter. If you disconnect or die partway, the attempt is tracked server-side; a still-active attempt can be resumed, otherwise you restart after the retry delay. Fighting mobs in this dungeon gives no drops or vanilla XP - it exists only for the quest.

sections.heading: The knight trial
sections.body: Killing Igris starts the advancement phase for you and every party member who is in the dungeon with you: 'BOSS SLAIN - Defeat the summoned knights [0/50]'. Each qualifying knight kill grants one shared point to the party. When the counter fills, the vessel selection opens.

sections.heading: Choosing your vessel
sections.body: The selection screen lists all vessels. Work-in-progress vessels refuse with a 'WIP (Work in progress)' message. Taken vessels refuse with a server-limit message. Picking Ashborn plays an extra shadow presentation sequence before the quest finishes; every other pick finishes immediately with a 'VESSEL SELECTED' popup. Ruler picks are shown in aqua, Monarch picks in purple.

sections.heading: Failing and retrying
sections.body: Dying during the run fails the active attempt and cleans up the dungeon. You get a failure notice and can re-enter after 10 seconds. Operators can also re-open the quest for a player who already finished it, without touching the rest of their progression.

sections.heading: How the kit plays
sections.body: You kill things, extract their shadows with Arise, then summon them from storage. Summoning costs mana per shadow (see Shadow Types for costs); dismissing returns them. Shadows keep their level, rank, equipment and even carried items between summons, and boss shadows slowly regenerate saved health (1 HP per second) while stored. Shadows automatically pick up mana stone drops from their kills; the items drop back out if the shadow is dismissed or destroyed.

sections.heading: Shadow Command modes
sections.body: Five modes, applied to your whole summoned group: Default (fight what you fight and whatever attacks you, otherwise stay close), Protect (only attack direct threats to you), Berserk (freely hunt hostile mobs within 48 blocks), Follow (no combat at all), and Clear Dungeon (dungeon-only: the group fans out and sweeps every remaining enemy with coordinated pathing). Your own combat always takes priority - if you get hit or land a hit, shadows immediately peel onto that target regardless of mode.

sections.heading: Formations
sections.body: You can save the current positions of your summoned shadows as a named formation. It becomes a castable skill that re-summons the group in that arrangement around you. Formation names are capped at 24 characters.

sections.heading: Shadow Exchange
sections.body: After using Baran's runestone you can save up to 7 anchors (a location tied to one of your basic shadow types) and later teleport to one. Casting has a 1.2 second delay and a 4 second cooldown, works across dimensions, and consumes the anchor on arrival. You cannot set anchors inside dungeons or castle dimensions.

sections.heading: Monarch's Domain and the Black Heart
sections.body: With Monarch's Domain earned, hold sneak for about 3.5 seconds to charge, then release a wave: every owned shadow within 50 blocks gains Strength II, Speed II, Resistance II and Domain Boost II for 2.5 minutes (you take brief Slowness afterwards). At the very end of the story content, releasing the System at the Cartenon Temple grants the Shadow Monarch the Black Heart: a flat +100,000 maximum mana reservoir and the removal of the shadow storage ceiling. The mana grant deliberately does not raise ability costs - costs are computed from your Intelligence-based pool only.

sections.heading: How to cast
sections.body: Kill something that leaves a shadow soul or a boss corpse, stand within 18 blocks, and cast Arise. The skill raises as many souls as your free storage and mana allow in one cast, most valuable first (Beru > Kaisel > Igris > Tusk > High Orc > Bear > Orc > Knight > Lycan > Goblins). If some are left behind, the message tells you whether storage or mana was the limit. Creative mode always succeeds and costs nothing.

sections.heading: The chance math
sections.body: Chance starts at 82% and drops 0.8% per level the target has over you, floored at 25% and capped at 96%. Targets at or below your level are near-certain. Because the third attempt on any corpse is guaranteed, a boss you personally earned can always be taken within three casts as long as it is within 75 levels of you.

sections.heading: Ownership and uniqueness
sections.body: Corpses are tagged to their killer: you can only extract bodies you have rights to. The four boss shadows (Igris, Beru, Tusk, Kaisel) are unique - once you own one, further copies of that boss cannot be extracted.

sections.heading: Why cost is a percentage
sections.body: Arise charges a share of your Intelligence-derived pool, not a flat number, so it stays meaningful at every build. Extra souls in the same cast cost less than the first (7% vs 15%), which makes raising a pile of corpses at once cheaper than raising them one by one. The Black Heart's +100,000 reservoir never inflates this cost - it is computed from the Intelligence pool only.

sections.heading: How shadows earn XP
sections.body: Each enemy builds one XP pool from its stats (health, attack, armor, toughness, level; bosses x2.5 +40, elites x1.5, passive animals x0.25, capped at 100,000). When it dies, every contributing shadow receives the share of the pool matching the damage it actually dealt. A player or another shadow landing the killing blow does not erase earlier contributions. Levelling past the current cap is impossible - the cap follows your own level.

sections.heading: Unique bosses
sections.body: Igris, Beru, Tusk and Kaisel are extracted from their boss corpses and are strictly one-per-player. Kamish exists as the strongest shadow type in code, but is only granted through admin items, not normal play. Iron is a unique single-slot shadow as well; no normal acquisition path for it is present in code.

sections.heading: Customization
sections.body: Igris and Tusk can be handed a weapon item to hold. Every type can be assigned an outline glow color from the summon menu (stored per type, so the whole species matches). Shadows can be renamed via their roster entries and are auto-named otherwise ('Lycan 3', 'Igris').

sections.heading: Keeping them alive
sections.body: Shadow healing costs 1 MP per 4 HP restored, and you can restore just bosses or the whole summoned group in one click; the server recomputes cost when the packet lands, so a stale tooltip can never underpay. Boss shadows that despawn keep their saved health and regenerate 1 HP per second while stored.

sections.heading: What manifestation changes
sections.body: While manifested, almost every skill in the vessel's kit gets a stronger version: bigger radii and ranges, extra charges or targets, shorter cooldowns, higher damage ratios. sections.heading: Upkeep and ending
sections.body: Sustained forms (Frost, White Flame, Antares) drain mana every second and collapse on their own the moment you cannot pay, with a message telling you why. The armor-based manifestations (Shadow, Goliath) are temporary armor sessions: your previous armor is stored and returned when the form ends, and the session is force-ended if your vessel changes.

nodes.title: Gates
nodes.tagline: Portals that open near players and lead into dungeons
nodes.summary: Gates appear in the Overworld near a random player on a world timer. Right-click one to enter its dungeon. If nobody clears a gate in time, it can break and dump its monsters into your world.

facts.label: Spawn timer
facts.value: One spawn attempt after soloGateDelay seconds (default 400, ~6.7 min); timer resets to 0 when a gate appears

facts.label: Spawn location
facts.value: Within 200 blocks of a random Overworld player, on dry solid ground (12 site attempts, water rejected)

facts.label: First gate
facts.value: The first natural gate in a world is always Gate - Goblin Sewers

facts.label: Lifetime
facts.value: 24,000 ticks (one full Minecraft day) before the gate vanishes

facts.label: Chat notice
facts.value: Broadcast with exact X/Y/Z coordinates (toggle: soloGateNotification, default on)

facts.label: Entry

facts.label: Cleared gates

sections.heading: How gates appear
sections.body: A world timer counts up one point per second. When it reaches the soloGateDelay gamerule (default 400), the mod tries to place a gate near a random Overworld player: it picks a spot up to 200 blocks away, checks that the ground is solid and dry, and spawns the gate there. If it cannot find a safe dry spot after 12 tries, it waits for the next timer cycle. A successful spawn resets the timer and (by default) announces the gate's coordinates in chat. Gate spawning can be disabled with the soloGateSpawning gamerule.

sections.heading: What can spawn
sections.body: After the guaranteed first Goblin Sewers gate, every spawn is a weighted roll. Approximate weights: Procedural Gate 150, custom datapack dungeon gate 100 (only if custom dungeons are installed), Gate - Giant Spider 137, Gate - Lush Cave 114, Gate - Ancient Golem Cave 95, Gate - Goblin Sewers 75, Gate - Cemetery 66, Gate - Throne Room 59, Gate - Ant Nest 47, Red Gate 33. With the default soloLevelingRankedGates rule on, gates above your unlocked rank are removed from the table entirely (Sewers needs D, Giant Spider and Ancient Golem need C, Lush/Cemetery/Red Gate need B, Lab and Throne Room need A, Ant Nest needs S). Only one Red Gate can exist at a time.

sections.heading: Entering and leaving
sections.body: Right-click a gate to enter. Your return position is saved first, and any party members standing within 10 blocks of the gate are pulled in with you. Procedural gates generate their dungeon on first entry, which can take a few seconds ('Stabilizing the gate...'). Clearing the dungeon (killing its boss) opens a Dungeon Exit Portal back to the Overworld. A gate you cleared is written to a permanent world list and tells you 'This gate has already been cleared.' if you click it again.

sections.heading: Expiry and gate breaks
sections.body: An untouched gate ticks down for one full Minecraft day, then disappears. If the soloDungeonBreak gamerule is on (default), an expired gate can break: its boss and escort monsters spawn right where the gate stood. Gates you have already entered pause their countdown - except Red Gates, which are one-way and always keep counting down toward a break. See the Dungeon Break page for the exact chances.

nodes.title: Gate Ranks
nodes.tagline: E through S - how gate difficulty is decided and unlocked
nodes.summary: Every gate has a rank from E to S. Your hunter rank and level decide which ranks can spawn for you, and the rank decides how big, how deep, and how dangerous the dungeon behind the gate is.

facts.label: Ranks
facts.value: E, D, C, B, A, S (numeric 1-6)

facts.label: Level floors
facts.value: Your level alone unlocks: D at 15, C at 30, B at 50, A at 75, S at 100

facts.label: Certified rank
facts.value: A higher certified Hunter Rank from evaluation also counts; vessels always count as S

facts.label: Rooms per rank
facts.value: E 7, D 8, C 10, B 12, A 14, S 16 (procedural default room counts)

facts.label: Mob pack size
facts.value: E/D/C 2, B 3, A 2, S 3 mobs per pack marker

facts.label: Rank dimensions
facts.value: E/D runs share dungeon_dimension_d; C, B, A, S each use their own dimension

facts.label: E/D easing
facts.value: E-rank mobs: 65% health, 55% damage. D-rank mobs: 80% health, 70% damage

sections.heading: How your unlocked rank is computed
sections.body: With ranked gates on (the default), the game takes the higher of two numbers: your certified Hunter Rank from evaluations, and a floor based on your level (D at level 15, C at 30, B at 50, A at 75, S at 100). If you carry a Monarch vessel, you always count as S. Gates whose minimum rank is above that number simply never spawn for you.

sections.heading: How a procedural gate picks its rank
sections.body: In ranked worlds the gate rolls a rank at or below your ceiling, weighted toward the top: your exact rank has weight 40, one below 28, two below 17, anything lower 9. With ranked gates turned off, every world rolls from an open table that leans hard toward the high end: E 4, D 7, C 13, B 22, A 28, S 26.

sections.heading: What rank changes inside
sections.body: Rank sets the procedural dungeon's shape: default room count grows from 7 (E) to 16 (S), rooms get bigger (E rooms 11-13 blocks, S rooms 19-27, boss rooms up to 31), ceilings get taller, and mob packs get larger. Rank also routes you to a dimension: E and D share one introductory dimension where mobs are deliberately weakened (E mobs deal 55% damage with 65% health; D mobs 70% damage with 80% health) so early gates stay survivable.

sections.heading: Rank and gate breaks
sections.body: Rank also matters when a gate expires: a gate at or below the best online player's rank always breaks, while a gate above everyone's rank only breaks some of the time. Details are on the Dungeon Break page.

nodes.title: Dungeon Break
nodes.tagline: Ignore a gate long enough and its monsters come to you
nodes.summary: A gate that expires without being cleared can break, spawning its boss and escort monsters in the Overworld right where the gate stood. Whether it breaks depends on how the gate's rank compares to the strongest online hunter.

facts.label: Trigger
facts.value: Gate expires after 24,000 ticks (one Minecraft day) without being cleared

facts.label: Master switch
facts.value: soloDungeonBreak gamerule, default true

facts.label: Guaranteed break
facts.value: Gate rank at or below the best online player's Hunter Rank: always breaks

facts.label: Above your rank
facts.value: 1 rank above: 65%. 2 above: 45%. 3 above: 30%. 4+ above: 18%

facts.label: Repeat protection
facts.value: Each break of the same gate type subtracts 15 points (up to 4 stacks); chance never drops below 5%; a quiet expiry refunds one stack

facts.label: Story mode
facts.value: Story mode's intro grace period suppresses breaks entirely

facts.label: Manual trigger
facts.value: /slr OP DungeonBreak (admin, permission 3) force-expires gates within 64 blocks

sections.heading: What actually breaks out
sections.body: Each gate type has its own breach roster, roughly the dungeon's population in miniature. Examples verified in code: an expired Goblin Sewers gate releases the Goblin King with goblin clubs, archers and a mage; the Ant Nest gate releases Beru with a swarm of red ants; a Red Gate releases Baruka with ice elves and giant polar bears; a procedural gate releases goblins, green orcs and gem golems. Datapack (custom) gates never break - they just vanish.

sections.heading: The break roll
sections.body: When an unentered gate hits its one-day lifetime, the game compares the gate's rank to the highest Hunter Rank among online players. If the gate is at or below that rank it always breaks - the assumption is someone could have handled it. If it outranks everyone, the chance drops with the gap: 65% one rank above, 45% two above, 30% three above, 18% beyond that. The world also remembers recent breaks per gate type and knocks 15 percentage points off per remembered break (max 4 remembered), never going below 5%, so the same gate type will not chain-break endlessly.

sections.heading: Red Gates always count down
sections.body: Normal gates stop their expiry countdown once someone enters them. Red Gates do not: they are one-way, so their sealed entrance keeps aging and will eventually break if the run inside is abandoned. Keep that in mind before walking away from one.

sections.body: Use the party GUI or the compatibility commands: /Party Create <name> (optionally with a password) and /Party Join <name>. Join requests you send expire after two minutes. The interface shows parties near you (within 96 blocks) so you can request a spot without typing names.

sections.heading: Parties and gates
sections.body: When one member right-clicks a gate, every party member standing within 10 blocks of that gate is teleported in as well - this applies to normal procedural gates and Red Gates. In wave arenas, monster counts scale up for every extra member and the encounter level is the party's average, so bring people close to your level.

sections.heading: Parties and PvP quests
sections.body: Party membership is also how the System decides who is friend and foe. Attacking someone in your own party or guild never triggers a Killing Intent urgent quest against you - but if you attack an outsider, their retaliation quest targets your entire party.

nodes.title: Red Gates
nodes.tagline: One-way wave gauntlets ending in Baruka
nodes.summary: A Red Gate seals behind you the moment you enter. Inside is an instanced arena in a frozen realm where waves of monsters attack, ending with the Ice Elf boss Baruka. The exit portal stays locked until the boss falls.

facts.label: Natural spawn
facts.value: Weight 33 in the gate table, needs rank B in ranked worlds; only one Red Gate active at a time

facts.label: Surprise transformation
facts.value: A procedural gate of rank B or higher has a 2% chance to turn red when first opened

facts.label: Realm
facts.value: All Red Gates share sololeveling:dungeon_dimension_snow, split into private 1024-block arena cells

facts.label: Waves
facts.value: Frost: ice bears (3), then ice elves 4 / 6 / 8 / 6-elite, then Baruka. Other territories skip the bear wave

facts.label: Party scaling
facts.value: Each extra member adds roughly half a wave's base count, capped at 18 active mobs

facts.label: Timing
facts.value: First wave 5s after arrival; 8s between waves; 10s boss intro

facts.label: Arena barrier

facts.label: Exit
facts.value: Dungeon Exit Portal spawns locked and only opens when the run is complete

sections.heading: How you end up in one
sections.body: Two ways. A dedicated Red Gate can spawn naturally once you can roll rank-B gates (the advancement 'No Way Back' marks surviving the other way: any procedural gate of rank B or above has a 2% chance to seal into a Red Gate at the moment your group opens it). Both routes are blocked while another Red Gate is already active in the world. Party members within 10 blocks are dragged in with the opener.

sections.heading: The arena
sections.body: You arrive in a private, snow-covered arena cell prepared just for your group - terrain, scenery and ice shards are generated per run from the instance seed. A barrier at 80 blocks bounces you back to the center if you try to walk out, and wave monsters that stray past 76 blocks are leashed back in. Which of the eight Monarch territories the gate belongs to changes the landscape palette and the difficulty scaling (see Monarch Territories).

sections.heading: The waves
sections.body: Frost-territory gates (the starter kind) run six encounters: an ice bear rush, four escalating ice elf waves (the fourth is an elite guard), then Baruka. Other territories cut the bear wave and start straight at the elf vanguard. Wave counts scale with party size and the whole arena is capped at 18 active wave mobs. Baruka is worth 5,000 base XP; ice elves 35; giant polar bears 16 (from the mob pool data).

sections.heading: Getting out
sections.body: The exit portal exists from the start but stays locked until the boss encounter completes. Finishing the run marks the gate cleared, unlocks the portal, and frees the world to spawn a new Red Gate. Using /solodungeonstuck from inside is treated as abandonment, not a clear - the empty arena is torn down and the sealed gate outside keeps aging toward a dungeon break.

nodes.title: Monarch Territories
nodes.tagline: Eight Monarch domains that flavor every Red Gate
nodes.summary: Every Red Gate belongs to one of eight Monarch territories: Destruction, Frost, Fangs, Plagues, Iron Body, White Flames, Transfiguration, and Beginning. The territory sets the arena's terrain and its difficulty scaling, and there is a creative-mode gate egg for each.

facts.label: The eight
facts.value: Destruction, Frost, Fangs, Plagues, Iron Body, White Flames, Transfiguration, Beginning

facts.label: Frost is the starter
facts.value: Frost arenas clamp the encounter level to 0-10 regardless of party level

facts.label: Other territories
facts.value: Encounter level = party average (minimum 1, fallback 35 when no level is found)

facts.label: Dedicated Red Gates
facts.value: Default to Frost unless tagged otherwise

facts.label: Transformed gates
facts.value: A procedural gate that turns red gets a territory derived from its UUID - effectively random among the eight

facts.label: Gate spawn eggs
facts.value: One 'Gate' spawn egg per territory (creative tab only); tooltip: 'Wave-based red gate encounter.'

facts.label: Arena cells
facts.value: Shared snow realm, one 1024-block lane per territory, up to 256 reusable instance slots

sections.heading: What territory actually changes
sections.body: All eight territories currently share the Red Gate wave roster (ice elves and Baruka; Frost adds the opening ice bear rush). What changes is the arena itself - each territory has its own terrain shaping and block palette - and the difficulty: Frost is the tutorial territory, hard-capped at encounter level 10, while every other territory scales the monsters to your party's average level with no such cap. In short: a Frost gate is safe practice; a Destruction or Beginning gate at high level is not.

sections.heading: The eight territory gates
sections.body: The mod registers a Red Gate spawn egg for each territory (monarch_territory_destruction_gate_spawn_egg, ..._frost_..., ..._fangs_..., ..._plagues_..., ..._iron_body_..., ..._white_flames_..., ..._transfiguration_..., ..._beginning_...). These are creative/admin items - they do not drop in survival. Placing one spawns a Red Gate entity pre-tagged with that exact territory, so map makers and server admins can stage a specific Monarch's gauntlet on demand. In survival play you get territories the natural way: dedicated Red Gates are Frost, and surprise-transformed gates roll a random territory.

sections.heading: Where the arenas live
sections.body: Every territory's arenas share one realm (dungeon_dimension_snow). Internally it is a grid far from the old terrain: territories occupy parallel lanes 1,024 blocks apart on the X axis and each concurrent run gets its own slot along Z, so runs never see each other. This is bookkeeping you normally never notice - but it explains why coordinates inside a Red Gate look enormous.

Admins can teleport in, read their position with /slr rift info, and even have the Boreal Crown - a 129 x 177 Frost Monarch fortress - built inside the Frost slice via the /slr structure command. The rift's fog and end-style sky are also in.

Treat everything on this page as a preview of where the Monarch territory system is heading; the eight territories you can actually fight in today are the Red Gate arenas.

nodes.title: Urgent Quests
nodes.tagline: Surprise objectives the System drops on you mid-dungeon
nodes.summary: While you are inside a dungeon, the System can suddenly issue an urgent quest: a timed kill sweep, a speed clear, or a no-skills challenge. Completing it adds XP to your System Rewards; leaving the dungeon or running out of time fails it.

facts.label: Trigger chance
facts.value: 35% per new dungeon run, rolled once when you enter; 55% in procedural dungeons and Red Gates

facts.label: Quest kinds
facts.value: Kill (timed family sweep), Clear (beat the boss within 300s), No Skills (beat the boss without using any skill)

facts.label: Kill target safety
facts.value: Target is capped by living mobs actually present, minus headroom of at least 2 (or 20%); if fewer than 6 kills are possible, no kill quest is offered

facts.label: Failure
facts.value: Leaving the dungeon, timing out, or using a skill on a no-skills quest fails instantly

facts.label: XP rewards
facts.value: 180-480 XP depending on dungeon and quest (e.g. Goblin Extermination 180, Kargalgan no-skills 480)

facts.label: PvP variant

sections.heading: Dungeon urgent quests
sections.body: Every dungeon has its own quest pool. Examples straight from the code: Goblin Sewers offers 'Goblin Extermination' (kill 20 goblins in 100 seconds, 180 XP), 'Sewer Boss Rush' (clear within 300 seconds, 220 XP) and 'Weapon Only' (clear without skills, 260 XP). The cemetery, lab, lush gate, golem halls, Kargalgan's throne, the ant island, Red Gates and generic dungeons each have equivalent sets, scaling up to 480 XP for clearing Kargalgan's throne skill-less. Kill quests only count untamed, non-boss dungeon mobs from the right family in your own run, and progress pops up on your first kill and every fifth.

sections.heading: The kill-count guarantee
sections.body: Kill targets are honest: before offering 'Kill 20 goblins', the System counts the goblins actually alive in your instance and keeps at least 20% of them (never fewer than 2) as spare, in case a party member or the environment steals kills. If that math cannot leave you at least 6 kills, the kill quest is dropped from the pool and you get a clear or no-skills quest instead.

sections.heading: Killing Intent (PvP)
sections.body: If you enable PvP urgent quests, the System watches for real aggression against you from players outside your party and guild: a critical hit or class-skill damage triggers instantly, and three weapon hits inside 8 seconds also count. You then get 'Killing Intent': defeat the attacker and their whole online party. Dying to a target fails it. Your first-ever completion guarantees a runestone for a skill your attacker knows that you lack (retired and exclusive stones like Cold Blood excluded); later completions have a 35% runestone chance, falling back to 150-300 gold or 2-4 skill points. A fresh PvP quest cannot trigger within 60 seconds of the last one.

sections.heading: Kang Taeshik's ambush
sections.body: After you kill dungeon bosses, a hostile hunter named Kang Taeshik can be scheduled to ambush you. His quest is also called 'Killing Intent': defeat him and ensure your safety; dying fails it. Beating the ambush for the first time adds a Full Recovery to your System Rewards, plus a Stealth Runestone if you do not already know Stealth.

sections.heading: Story quests that use this system
sections.body: At the level cap the System issues 'The Way Back' (kneel - hold sneak - to open the way to the Cartenon Temple), followed inside by 'The Temple Wakes' (destroy the temple guardians) and 'The One Who Measured You' (destroy the Statue of God). These are scripted quests on the urgent-quest HUD rather than random rolls, and once the System has been released at the end of that arc, random urgent quests stop being issued.

Completing it puts the Demon King's Castle Key in your System Rewards. The key binds to whoever holds it first ('The key rejects your hand' for anyone else), only answers in the Overworld, and is consumed when it cracks the first seal and drops you on Floor 1. After that, return through the System GUI's castle button - it reads 'Demon King's Castle' outside and 'Castle Tower' inside.

sections.heading: The climb
sections.body: Floors 2 through 19 are kill-wave floors: defeat the floor's required count (12 on Floor 2 rising to 36 on Floor 19, with a spike of 32 before Vulcan on Floor 10) while the castle keeps 7-12 enemies active around you. Wave demons target you specifically and are leashed to your floor - they recover or despawn rather than getting stuck. Clearing a floor unlocks the next; your run, floor unlocks, and current floor all persist through logouts, deaths, and even the old castle layout (stranded players are migrated and teleported to their highest legitimate floor on login).

sections.heading: Floors worth knowing
sections.body: The named floors run: Ashen Threshold, Cinder Streets, Charred Gardens, Broken Aqueduct, Furnace Ward, Iron Foundry, Blood Market, Chain Barracks, Magma Reservoir, Vulcan's Crucible, Obsidian Causeway, Black Cathedral, Demon Archives, Furnace Spires, Radiru Castle, Storm Ramparts, Thunder Galleries, Crown Approach, Sky Throne Antechamber, and Baran's Tempest Throne. Floors 1, 10, 15 and 20 have their own pages.

sections.heading: After the summit
sections.body: Conquering all 20 floors marks the castle finished; its gates 'stay silent' if you try the key again. If you spared House Radiru on Floor 15, the castle button becomes 'Radiru Castle' and keeps taking you back to the sanctuary you protected. Slaughter them and the tower seals behind you for good.

sections.heading: The choice
sections.body: Beat down the castle's defenders and the gate opens with Esil waiting inside. Talking to her opens a mercy prompt. Spare her and the Pact of House Radiru is sealed: you receive the Entry Permit, the floor counts as cleared, and 'Radiru blood may no longer be spilled here' - every resident becomes invulnerable to you. Kill them instead and you still clear the floor and get the permit, plus the exclusive Cold Blood runestone and a 2,500 XP execution bonus on top of the floor's 1,500.

sections.heading: Why mercy pays later
sections.body: The pact turns Floor 15 into a persistent sanctuary: residents return, training dummies appear (they show your real post-mitigation damage per hit and reset to full health, making them the castle's DPS meter), and after you conquer Floor 20 the System's castle button becomes 'Radiru Castle' - a permanent home inside the tower. Slaughter the house and the conquered tower seals shut behind you forever. The Cold Blood runestone is the only thing mercy costs you; it is deliberately excluded from every other reward pool.

sections.body: Baran's melee is modest at 16 raw, but his abilities escalate in phase two: ground slams jump from 17 to 22 raw (with 8-10 ripple damage and 6-damage third waves), charges hit up to 21 on impact, and his magic blast rises from 18 to 24 raw. sections.heading: Cashing in
sections.body: Each crystal is a one-click gold voucher: right-click with it in hand and the gold is added to your System balance ('+320 gold'). The conversion is server-side and refuses non-System players, so you cannot pre-farm value before awakening. Crystals stack to 64 and are shiny in the inventory - hard to lose track of.

sections.heading: The deposit block
sections.body: Mana Crystal Deposits are jagged mineable outcrops ('A natural concentration of crystallized mana'). Breaking one with at least an iron pickaxe yields one or two crystals weighted heavily toward E and D grade - an S crystal is a 1-in-200 entry on the loot table, so Fortune is worth bringing. Silk Touch preserves the deposit block instead, letting you relocate it. Where deposits generate is authored into dungeon structures rather than driven by a worldgen feature, so treat any you find inside a dungeon as part of that room's loot.

nodes.title: Recovery Commands
nodes.tagline: Stuck in a dungeon? These get you out
nodes.summary: The mod ships safety-hatch commands for broken runs: /solodungeonstuck returns any player to safety, and admins can wipe gates or reset stats. Use them when a dungeon genuinely breaks, not as a free escape.

facts.label: /solodungeonstuck
facts.value: Any player. Emergency exit from a dungeon binding: returns you to your saved entry point (or world spawn), clears your dungeon state

facts.label: Failure case
facts.value: Replies 'No active dungeon recovery point was found.' if you have no binding

facts.label: /soloresetportals
facts.value: Permission 3. Discards every loaded gate entity and resets the gate spawn timer

facts.label: /soloresetstats
facts.value: Permission 3. Runs the full stat reset routine on the caller

facts.label: /slr OP DungeonBreak
facts.value: Permission 3. Force-expires gates within 64 blocks (needs a gate nearby)

facts.label: Red Gate warning
facts.value: Emergency-exiting a Red Gate abandons the run - it never counts as a clear

sections.heading: When to use /solodungeonstuck
sections.body: If a dungeon fails to generate, an exit portal never appears, or you log back into a dead instance, run /solodungeonstuck. It works for anyone with an active dungeon binding: you are teleported to a verified-safe spot near where you entered the gate (falling back to world spawn if no entry point was saved), your gravity, momentum and fall damage are cleaned up, and every dungeon flag on your player is cleared so gates work again.

sections.heading: What it costs you
sections.body: The command is an abandonment, not a victory. In a Red Gate arena, the emptied instance is torn down, the gate outside stays sealed, and its countdown continues toward a possible dungeon break. In ordinary dungeons you simply lose the run and any active urgent quest fails with 'Dungeon left'.

sections.heading: Admin tools
sections.body: Operators (permission level 3) additionally have /soloresetportals, which despawns all currently loaded gates and restarts the spawn timer - useful after a mod update leaves broken portal entities - and /soloresetstats, which reruns the stat reset routine. The /slr root also hides diagnostic and force tools like OP DungeonBreak and rift info behind the same permission level. There is also a passive safety net: players stranded in the old Demon King's Castle layout are automatically migrated to the shared realm at login.

nodes.title: Runestones
nodes.tagline: Right-click stones that teach you a skill, no class required
nodes.summary: Runestones are single-use items that teach one ability when you right-click them. They ignore your class, style, and rank. A skill learned from a runestone is permanent and survives class changes.

facts.label: Registered runestone items
facts.value: 114 items with the runestone_ id prefix, plus named stones (Murderious Intent Stone, Telekinesis Stone, Stealth Stone)

facts.label: How to use
facts.value: Right-click. The stone is consumed and the skill is added to your skill list

facts.label: Duplicate protection
facts.value: If you already know the skill, the stone refuses and is not consumed

facts.label: Class requirement
facts.value: None. Code comment: "Runestones are universal unlock items" and "Runestones are classless ability unlocks"

facts.label: Permanence
facts.value: A runestone marker is written to persistent player data, so the skill survives changing Hunter class or Mage specialization

facts.label: Creative tab
facts.value: A dedicated Runestones creative tab lists them all

facts.label: Retired stones
facts.value: Seven runestones with display names starting with "Retired" no longer teach anything (see Retired Runestones)

sections.heading: The universal rule
sections.body: This is the single most important thing about runestones: they bypass every normal gate. A Tanker can learn a Healer blessing. A Mage can learn Ghost Step. The Tanker runestones even print it on the tooltip: "Normal rank entitlement: X (the runestone bypasses rank)." Once learned, the game marks the skill as runestone-taught in your persistent data, so switching class or Mage specialization later never deletes it.

sections.heading: How you get them
sections.body: Runestones are reward items, not craftables. Verified sources in code: the Shadow Exchange Stone is a one-time reward for beating Baran legitimately; the Stealth Stone comes from an urgent quest; PvP urgent quests can award you a runestone copy of a skill the player you defeated knew (guaranteed on your first PvP quest clear, then a 35% chance per repeat, and Cold Blood is excluded from that pool); Telekinesis Stone is the first-kill reward for Blood-Red Commander Igris; Kasaka-related and boss advancement rewards deliver others through the System Rewards screen. Everything is also available from the Runestones creative tab.

sections.heading: One special case: Curse runestones
sections.body: Learning any Curse Mage delivery spell from a runestone automatically grants Curse Weave, the wheel that arms your curses. The wheel inherits the same runestone permanence, so you cannot end up with a curse delivery and no way to arm it.

sections.heading: Reading this section of the wiki
sections.body: The stones are grouped by the class whose kit they teach: Assassin, Mage (five specializations), Fighter (three styles), Tanker (two styles), Healer (two styles plus universal blessings), Ranger, and the Shadow Monarch stones. Remember that the grouping only tells you where the skill comes from, not who may learn it.

sections.heading: What the skills do
sections.body: From the in-game skill registry: Ghost Step gives two blink charges that Expose enemies you pass through. Night Rend teleports you behind the aimed target for a heavy opening cut. Flash Cut fans up to five targets with one shared damage budget. Dualwield is a two-dagger stance where every fourth hit crosses into nearby enemies. Critical Attack opens a counter window that evades, Exposes, and readies Riposte. Mutilation marks a target and detonates the cuts you recorded on it. Stealth vanishes you for four seconds behind a decoy; attacking from Stealth grants Ambush.

sections.heading: The stealth trio
sections.body: Shadow Feint leaves an attackable afterimage; if it gets hit you relocate to a flank, and recasting blinds and slows instead. Silent Domain places a dim zone where ordinary mobs drop their target and bosses are only delayed. Zero Presence is a short apex state with three Vanish charges, each spent only on a confirmed hit and granting no immunity.

sections.heading: The dangerous ones
sections.body: Cold Blood is a forbidden execution state that grows stronger with each kill while you keep landing hits. Murderious Intent projects killing intent that panics enemies weaker than you. Telekinesis Stone teaches you to move objects without touching them; in quest code it is also called Ruler's Hand.

sections.heading: How they differ from other runestones
sections.body: Mage stones plug into the staged spell system. The stone teaches the spell once; what the spell does afterward depends on your output stage, which rises with Hunter Rank and Intelligence. You do not need to be a Mage, and you do not need the matching specialization. The unlock is written with the same runestone marker as every other stone, so a later specialization change keeps the spell.

sections.heading: What each school plays like
sections.body: Fire is Scorch marks, explosions and area denial: Ignition Orb grows from an impact blast into a miniature sun, and Cremation executes marked enemies in a linked combustion chain. Barrier is constructs and control: walls that catch projectiles, prisms that imprison Fractured targets, and Absolute Bastion enclosing the battlefield in a fortress. Arcane is spatial precision: collision-safe teleports, gravity nodes, orbiting mana blades, and cutting space itself with Dimensional Rend. Storm is Voltage and routing: mark enemies Conductive, designate a routing root with Lightning Rod, then chain and finish with Skybreaker or wear the storm with Tempest Incarnate. Curse is armed afflictions delivered through Hex Bolt, area bursts, lingering miasma fields, allies who carry your curse for you, and Culling detonating every curse you have placed at once.

sections.heading: Striker
sections.body: Close-range impact. Ground Slam is a radial hit in a 5-block radius on up to 8 targets with damage falling off toward the rim. Iron Knuckle charges one armored punch in three steps; releasing later hits far harder. Breaker Combo is an input-timed three-parter where looking down on the third input spikes the target instead of knocking it away. Meteor Fist leaps to a point and lands an impact plus shockwave, failing for free if there is no safe landing. Titan's Barrage locks one target into 12 rising strikes and a launching finisher. Cross Strike throws two merging fist arcs; the second carries the guard damage that builds Impact.

sections.heading: Swordsman
sections.body: Movement cuts and finishers. Slash Dash sweeps one cut along a collision-safe dash, sharing a budget across up to 4 targets. Slash Fury delivers 5 ordered slashes while you are slowed but not frozen. Sword Beam launches a slash-shaped wave piercing up to 3 targets. Sword Dance marks a target and flank-steps on each confirmed hit, up to 4 steps. Radiant Execution draws and delivers one precision line cut with bonus damage below 30% health, spending Sword Tempo. Sword of Light is a luminous stance planting Light Seals that can launch sealed enemies or convert into a beam. Watch the shop: two different stones both display as "Cross Strike Stone" - one teaches the sword version, one the fist version.

sections.heading: Mutant (in-game name: Mutant)
sections.body: The beast tree. Magical Eye reveals enemies below 70% health and their weak points. Claw Strikes is a three-swipe chain that applies Rend; looking down on the last swipe focuses it. Beast Sense briefly heightens speed and awareness and improves Feral gain. Predator Rush bounds onto a wounded target and mauls it, with bonus damage at 3 Rend stacks. Partial Transformation is a maintained hybrid form (40 Feral to enter, cheaper to hold above 60 Feral). Full Beast Transformation commits 80 Feral to a time-limited full beast form.

sections.heading: Sentinel: the shield tree
sections.body: Shield Bash lunges into one target with an offhand shield equipped - you need an actual shield in your offhand - and one Bash can relieve active Willpower Strain. Taunt and Tank Leap build Iron Wall stacks. Reinforcement braces for the next hit and then enters a shorter reinforced stance. Willpower delays incoming damage as Strain that must be settled later; the skill registry warns that Strain cannot be erased by logging out or changing class. Protection Mark anchors a shared-integrity zone that spends its integrity to protect allies.

sections.heading: Juggernaut: the mass tree
sections.body: Heavy Blow trades modest damage for heavy displacement and guard pressure. Iron Body converts a hit taken in the first moment into extra Poise. Seismic Grapple pins normal targets but only drags and slows bosses and players. Gigantification spends 35 Poise on a heavy maintained form that gets cheaper to hold above 50 Poise. Colossus Charge gathers enemies along an armored rush and releases them at the end. Mountain Breaker is a two-stage impact - outward lift, then inward collapse - where Poise pays part of the cost but never all of it.

sections.heading: Why these tooltips matter
sections.body: The Sentinel stones are the clearest in-game statement of the universal runestone rule. Each one prints "Normal rank entitlement: X (the runestone bypasses rank)." An E-rank Hunter holding the Protection Mark stone can learn an S-rank skill on the spot.

sections.heading: Saint: focused rescue
sections.body: Heal Beam channels restoration into one ally (self-cast at reduced efficiency). Haste Buff and Physical Buff raise an ally's speed or physical output and widen to two allies at higher Intelligence. Purification removes harmful effects and is free if there is nothing to remove. Overheal converts healing you actually wasted into absorption. Blessing Mark banks healing on an ally and releases it automatically if they drop below 30% health.

sections.heading: Shepherd: group rescue
sections.body: Healing Pulse needs no target and heals you plus the most wounded allies nearby, pulsing twice at the highest Intelligence stage. Purifying Wave cleanses and lightly heals everyone including you. Guardian Step dashes to an ally and shields you both, failing for free without a safe landing. Sanctuary is a bounded healing field that adds stagger resistance at higher Intelligence. Second Wind is the emergency button: party recovery weighted by missing health, cleansing one control effect and granting recovery protection. Camouflage drops threat and turns you translucent to reposition.

sections.heading: The universal blessings
sections.body: Guardian Ward layers damage resistance, then fire resistance, then absorption. Mana Font restores an ally's mana pool. Vitality Surge raises maximum health and heals into the new room. Divine Favor is the capstone: several boons at once, with the ally count rising with Intelligence. Because runestones ignore class, these four are popular pickups for non-Healers.

High Value Target marks one enemy for stronger precision damage and extra Focus gain. Sharpshooter fires a piercing Sunder Shot that exposes enemy defenses. Hawkeye reveals visible hostiles in your aiming cone.
